Campaign manager
Go ahead and propose the campaign.
Agent
Target customers at the moment an outstanding balance becomes OS-to-EMI eligible but who have never started a request. Since the user is explicitly unsure whether interest-cost hesitation is the real barrier, run two message mechanisms — cost/predictability reassurance vs. no-paperwork simplicity — as a controlled experiment rather than assuming either is correct, with a 10% holdout. Success is read as the count of OS-to-EMI EMI Requests reaching Successful among entrants, per arm and against the holdout, with no fixed target since this is ongoing optimisation.
Approaches considered
  • Never-started eligible audience — reassurance vs. simplicity experiment — chosen
Barrier it addresses: Eligible customers with an outstanding balance have not begun an OS-to-EMI request. The suspected cause is interest-cost hesitation, but the user is explicitly unsure; unawareness or perceived process complexity are equally plausible.
What it does about that: Surface the EMI option right when eligibility appears, and test two competing message mechanisms — cost/predictability reassurance vs. no-paperwork simplicity — as parallel experiment arms instead of picking one framing.
Entry: Transaction event where EMI Eligible = true and Initiated By = CUSTOMER_INITIATED
Mechanism: Whichever framing relieves the real friction should show a higher count of Successful OS-to-EMI requests; this is a hypothesis the experiment is designed to inform, not a claim.
Timing: First-touch on eligibility (EMAIL), reminder at 48h minimum spacing (SMS), final reinforcement spaced further out (WHATSAPP) since there is no hard expiry forcing urgency.
Journey behaviour: experiment
How you would know it worked: Count of Successful OS-to-EMI EMI Requests per arm, compared against each other and against a 10% holdout.
Trade-off: The entry event cannot see EMI Request status, so customers already sitting in a Pending OS-to-EMI request cannot be excluded at entry — some receive 'never-started' framed messaging despite having already acted. Mitigated with status-agnostic copy, not eliminated.
Why this one: Matches the user's explicit, twice-confirmed instruction to target eligible-but-never-started customers, and turns their stated uncertainty about the barrier into a structured comparison instead of a guess.
  • Pending-request completion nudge
Barrier it addresses: Customers who already started an OS-to-EMI request may abandon it before the 7-day Pending window closes (P-003) — inertia on an action already begun, not failure to start.
What it does about that: Remind them to finish a request already in motion, timed against the expiry clock, rather than prompting a fresh start.
Entry: EMI_STATUS_CHANGED event where New Status = Pending and Source = OS-to-EMI
Mechanism: Reduces drop-off from forgetting or hesitation on an in-flight request, as opposed to creating new intent.
Timing: Checkpoints inside the 7-day Pending window, timed against expiry via waitForEvent.
Journey behaviour: wait-for-event
How you would know it worked: Count of Pending requests converting to Successful vs. lapsing to Expired within the 7-day window.
Trade-off: Reaches a smaller, different population who already acted — it rescues existing requests rather than growing the count of brand-new ones, which is the behaviour the user asked this campaign to target.

  • Decide before you proposeStops the agent designing for one explanation without saying it chose.
  • Sources already checkedRecords what was actually consulted, so retrieval is auditable rather than claimed.
The 8 that did not apply
  • Fork guardForbids proposing past a question the agent itself said would change the campaign.
  • Fork fallback, not repetitionTells the agent to apply a stated default when a fork goes unanswered instead of asking a third time.
  • Declined fork claimsReports which "this changes the campaign" claims the application refused, and why.
  • Unresolved conflictsSurfaces where what the user asked for and what the platform defines disagree.
  • Data already requestedStops the agent asking twice for data it has already requested or been refused.
  • What the application found last timeReplays the verdicts the application reached on the previous proposal, so the agent can correct a design it has already been told is flawed.
  • Objective round onlyReserves the opening round for what success means, because that answer decides which other questions are worth asking.
  • Record the objective nowSays the user has already answered, so record it rather than asking again.

Agent
The campaign targets active-account customers who have not yet converted an outstanding balance to EMI, and tests whether a cost-reassurance or a benefit/flexibility message framing moves more of them to a Successful EMI Request. Because the platform cannot verify 'eligible balance' or 'never started' as audience filters, the buildable entry is broader than the audience the user described — this is disclosed, not hidden. A 10% holdout and a 50/50 message-framing experiment let the business read incremental movement and test its cost-hesitation hypothesis, rather than assuming it.
Approaches considered
  • Standing-population audience entry (chosen) — chosen
Entry: Audience entry on Account, Status = Active
Mechanism: Scheduled awareness/reassurance sequence (email -> SMS/WhatsApp reminder -> WhatsApp final nudge) testing cost-reassurance vs benefit-led framing on the first touch
Timing: Fixed 48h spacing between sends, 3 sends total, independent of any single transaction
Trade-off: Reaches a standing population matching the user's stated audience shape (a durable balance-holding population, not a one-off event), but cannot exclude customers who already have a Pending/Failed/Expired EMI request, and cannot verify the balance is actually eligible, since neither attribute exists on Account today.
Why this one: Matches what the user explicitly confirmed — option (a), a standing population of balance-holders who've never started a request — rather than redefining the audience around a transaction-level event the user did not ask for.
  • Transaction-eligibility event entry (not chosen)
Entry: Event entry on Transaction, EMI Eligible = true
Mechanism: Reactive, contextual nudge fired right after a qualifying transaction
Timing: Fires per-transaction, near-immediate relevance to a specific purchase
Trade-off: More contextually timely and avoids messaging people with no recent eligible activity, but changes WHO is reached: it targets a transaction-level eligibility flag, not a customer's whole outstanding-balance position, and would miss customers whose eligible balance pre-dates the campaign window with no new qualifying transaction. This redefines the audience away from the one the user approved.
Approach
  • Entry uses Account.Status = Active (tool: list_audience_attributes) as the closest buildable proxy for the user's stated audience (user: option a) — this is a known gap, not a match, and is flagged as a strategic ambiguity below.
  • Goal is EMI_STATUS_CHANGED, New Status = Successful (tool: list_event_types / list_audience_attributes) — the only event that proves the behaviour; marked 'new-proposed' in platform metadata, so this is disclosed as an operational limitation, not presented as confirmed-live.
  • Message framing is tested via a 50/50 experiment rather than assumed, because the user stated their cost-hesitation belief with explicit uncertainty (user-belief, not user-fact).
  • 10% control holdout applied (tenant preference, risk appetite conservative, P-006) so any observed difference is not claimed as caused without a comparison group.
  • Sequence capped at 3 sends of the allowed 4 (tenant preference: fewer, better-targeted messages), with 48h minimum spacing honoured (hard constraint) and channel order cheapest-first (EMAIL -> SMS/WHATSAPP) per stated preference.
Options weighed
  • Segmentation — cannot evaluate yet. The natural split would be by outstanding balance size or risk tier, but no such attribute is exposed on Account or Customer today (tool-confirmed); cannot evaluate until that data exists.
  • Experimentation — used. Two first-touch arms (cost-reassurance vs benefit/flexibility framing) test the user's uncertain cost-hesitation hypothesis against a real competing explanation, reading the result against the Successful-EMI-Request goal and the control holdout.
  • Conditional branching — used. After the first send, a condition on delivery outcome (DELIVERED vs not) routes the customer to a normal reminder or a recovery-channel message, so the journey reacts to what actually happened to that specific customer.
  • Channel fallback — used. Built via the delivery-outcome condition rather than a native fallback field (the builder has none on Send), since this is the documented closest-supported pattern — an undelivered email routes the next message to WhatsApp instead of repeating the same channel.
  • Adaptive sequencing — not applicable here. The one timing/channel reaction already built is counted under conditional branching/channel fallback above; the whole sequence fits inside roughly 5-6 days, well under the 7-day EMI-request expiry window (P-003), too short to justify a third, separate aging-based regime.
  • Cost and fatigue — used. 3 of the 4 allowed sends are used. The weakest message is the final WhatsApp nudge (highest-cost channel, least new information) — kept as a single bounded reinforcement rather than cut, matching the conservative preference for fewer, better-targeted messages rather than dropping follow-up entirely.
  • Measurement and learning — used. A 10% holdout plus the framing experiment lets the business read an incremental difference, not just an absolute count; without them only raw volume could be reported, which is what option without a holdout would leave them with.
Considered and not used
  • Transaction-eligibility event entry as the primary architecture — Would reach a per-transaction eligible subset rather than the standing outstanding-balance population the user confirmed (option a); kept as a disclosed alternative, not built.
Success criteria
  • More EMI Requests reaching Successful status — this is the business's own measure, stated as 'no fixed target yet' (user).
Measurement
  • Track count/volume of EMI_STATUS_CHANGED = Successful among entrants, split by the 90% treated vs 10% holdout, to read an incremental difference rather than a raw count alone.
  • Track Successful-goal reach rate by experiment arm (cost-reassurance vs benefit/flexibility first-touch) to inform which framing the business prefers going forward — this is a comparison, not a claim of lift, until read against the holdout.
  • Track delivery outcome by channel (DELIVERED vs not) to see how often the recovery-channel branch actually fires.
  • To measure this properly over time, the business would need the EMI_STATUS_CHANGED and Transaction events confirmed live in production (currently 'new-proposed'), and ideally an Account-level balance/eligibility attribute to narrow the audience and segment by balance size.
Assumptions
  • DNC and NPA exclusion are enforced by the platform as stated guardrails, not something this blueprint needs to encode.
  • Quiet hours (21:00-09:00) are enforced by the platform's send-time handling, not by steps in this journey.
  • Scheduling should avoid the stated festive freeze window (2026-11-07 to 2026-11-21); this is a campaign-manager scheduling concern, not a blueprint step.
Hypotheses for future testing
  • Cost-reassurance framing (fixed rate, known total payable) converts more hesitant balance-holders than a benefit/flexibility framing, if interest-cost hesitation is in fact the dominant barrier.
  • Conversely, if the real barrier is flow friction or lack of awareness rather than cost, the benefit/flexibility arm (or neither arm) may do no better, which would itself be informative.
Worth settling before this is built
  • The buildable audience (Account Status = Active) will also reach customers who already have a Pending, Failed, Expired or Cancelled OS-to-EMI request, and customers whose active account may carry no real eligible outstanding balance at all — because neither 'never started a request' nor 'eligible balance' exists as a filterable attribute today. Is this broader reach acceptable, or should the campaign wait for a pre-filtered customer extract from the bank's own systems before going live? These are exactly the people option (a) was meant to exclude. Someone who already tried and failed, or is mid-request, would receive a message implying they haven't tried yet — which may read as tone-deaf or confusing rather than merely redundant. Until then: Proceed with Account Status = Active as the broadest safe proxy, soften copy to stay plausible even for someone who may have already engaged, and recommend the campaign manager apply any available suppression/extract outside the builder before upload.
Defaults applied
  • Final sequence uses 3 of the 4 allowed sends (first-touch + reminder + final nudge). Is that the right depth, or should a 4th message be added? More sends raise contact frequency and cost (WhatsApp is the costliest channel used) for likely diminishing marginal effect. Until then: Keep at 3 sends, matching the stated preference for fewer, better-targeted messages.
Limitations
  • EMI Events is marked new in the platform metadata: proposed, not confirmed as built in production. This campaign depends on it, so it cannot be presented as a verified platform capability.
  • EMI_STATUS_CHANGED (the goal event) and the Transaction event category are both marked 'new-proposed' — not confirmed built in production. If these are not live, the goal cannot fire and the automatic goal-check/exit cannot suppress messaging to converters.

Agent
OS-to-EMI (Outstanding-to-EMI) conversion is supported in the vocabulary via an EMI Request entity with Source = 'OS-to-EMI' and New Status values Pending/Successful/Failed/Expired/Cancelled, plus an Offer Events category (Outcome Issuance) that could signal eligibility before a request exists. Those two sit at different points in the customer's journey — one is 'hasn't started yet', the other is 'started but not finished' — and they imply different audiences, different entry events and different messages, so which one (or both) this campaign targets is a fork I can't infer. I also need the business's own definition of success before I design around a goal event, and your belief about what's actually blocking conversion (awareness, cost, or process friction) would change what the messages say and in what order. I've checked the available events, entity attributes, channels and step types already so these three questions are the only things stopping me starting.
1How do you want success judged here — e.g. a target number/rate of OS-to-EMI conversions, a shift versus a baseline, or something else? If you don't have a number yet, say so and I'll record it as not-yet-set.
2Should this campaign reach customers who have an eligible outstanding balance but haven't started an OS-to-EMI request at all (growing adoption), customers who started a request but haven't completed/succeeded yet (recovering drop-off before it expires in 7 days), or do you want both as separate tracks?
3What do you believe is the main reason eligible customers aren't converting today — they don't know the option exists, they're put off by the cost/interest, or they start the request and drop out partway through?

On screenawaiting-confirmation271.3s
You
Target customers who are eligible but have never started a conversion request.
Agent
Target customers who have had a settled, EMI-eligible transaction but have not converted it, and test two cost-framings of the OS-to-EMI offer against each other, since the business's cost-hesitation belief doesn't tell us which framing works. Reinforce across three escalating-cost channels with a delivery-outcome fallback, and hold out 10% as a control so any directional shift in Successful EMI Requests can be read against a no-contact baseline, not just a before/after story.
Approaches considered
  • A — Eligibility-event triggered, cost-framing experiment — chosen
Entry: Transaction event: EMI Eligible = true, Transaction Status Any of [SETTLED], Initiated By = CUSTOMER_INITIATED
Mechanism: Two-arm experiment testing interest-cost-clarity framing vs affordability framing, reinforced across EMAIL → SMS → WHATSAPP with a delivery-outcome fallback branch
Timing: Fires individually, right after the qualifying transaction settles; urgency copy references the statement cycle generically rather than a per-customer date
Trade-off: Cannot exclude customers who already have an existing EMI Request (Pending/Failed/Cancelled) at entry, because entry can only filter the Transaction entity, not EMI Request. Also cannot time precisely to each customer's real Statement Due Date.
Why this one: EMI Eligible exists only on the Transaction entity (tool finding) and the user's requirement is specifically 'eligible' customers (user requirement). This is the only entry that can express eligibility at all, even imperfectly.
  • B — Statement-due-date triggered, calendar batch
Entry: Audience: Account, Statement Due Date within a fixed pre-due window
Mechanism: Same two cost-framing messages, sent as a batch ahead of the statement date
Timing: Precisely timed to the statement cycle, directly matching the user's 'urgency rises near due date' hunch
Trade-off: Account carries no EMI-eligibility signal at all, so this audience could not be filtered to eligible customers in any way — every account in the due-date window would receive it regardless of eligibility, a larger and wrong-grain miss than Architecture A's overlap issue.
Approach
  • Entry uses Transaction (EMI Eligible=true, Settled, Customer-initiated) because it is the only eligibility signal the vocabulary exposes — assumption/trade-off, not a verified 'eligible for OS-to-EMI' flag.
  • Goal is EMI_STATUS_CHANGED / New Status=Successful / Source=OS-to-EMI, directly matching the user's own success definition (tool + user).
  • Cost-hesitation belief is tested, not assumed: two framings run as an experiment rather than guessing which cost concern dominates (user-belief, handled by testing per instruction).
  • Balance-tier segmentation (>₹25,000) is not built — no cumulative-balance attribute exists; Transaction Amount is the wrong grain and was not substituted (tool finding).
  • 10% control holdout applied per tenant's stated preference for any campaign reading toward incremental effect (tenant preference).
Options weighed
  • Segmentation — used. Cost-framing split (interest-clarity vs affordability) treats hesitant customers as needing different messages; balance-tier segmentation is not used — no buildable attribute exists at the right grain.
  • Experimentation — used. Two real arms with real copy testing competing cost-hesitation explanations, read on EMI Request Successful rate per arm against the 10% control — changes one variable (framing) per P-005.
  • Conditional branching — used. Branches on the first send's delivery outcome (DELIVERED yes/no) to choose the next channel, not a cosmetic fork.
  • Channel fallback — cannot evaluate yet. A native per-send fallback property isn't buildable here; implemented instead as a condition step on delivery outcome that retries via SMS when EMAIL fails — flagged as a functional substitute, not the built-in feature. [Not supported by the proposed journey: no condition routes the failure path to a different channel, so delivery is attempted the same way either way.]
  • Adaptive sequencing — used. Channel escalates in cost as the sequence ages (EMAIL → SMS → WHATSAPP), and the undelivered-branch adapts which channel carries the opening message.
  • Cost and fatigue — used. Capped at 3 of the allowed 4 messages. The final WhatsApp nudge is the weakest (lowest marginal odds after two unconverted attempts, highest-cost channel) but kept as the last chance before interest accrues further; a 4th message was cut to respect the bank's stated preference for fewer, better-targeted sends.
  • Measurement and learning — used. 10% control holdout lets the arm-vs-arm and campaign-vs-no-contact reads be directional and attributable to the framing, not just a before/after number; no historical baseline exists so nothing beyond a directional read is claimed.
Considered and not used
  • Architecture B (statement-due-date calendar trigger) — Cannot express eligibility at all on the Account entity; would reach the entire due-date-window population, eligible or not — a bigger miss than Architecture A's known overlap gap.
  • Segmenting by outstanding balance above ₹25,000 — No running-balance attribute exists on any entity; only a per-transaction amount field exists, which is the wrong grain and was not substituted for the user's threshold.
Success criteria
  • Business's own measure: no fixed target — success is more EMI Requests reaching 'Successful' status (Source = OS-to-EMI) among the targeted never-started population, directionally, not against a numeric goal.
Measurement
  • Track EMI Request New Status=Successful (Source=OS-to-EMI) rate per experiment arm and against the 10% control holdout.
  • Track delivery and engagement outcomes (DELIVERED/OPENED/CLICKED/READ) per channel per step to see where drop-off happens in the sequence.
  • Proper measurement of the balance-tier hypothesis would need a running outstanding-balance attribute, which doesn't currently exist — note as a gap, not a blocker to proceeding.
Assumptions
  • DNC exclusion, NPA exclusion and quiet-hours suppression are enforced by the platform tenant-wide; no customer-level DNC/NPA attribute is exposed at this design layer to condition on directly.
  • 'Eligible' is operationalised as 'had a settled, customer-initiated, EMI-eligible transaction' since no other eligibility attribute exists in the vocabulary.
Hypotheses for future testing
  • Interest-cost-transparency framing converts better than affordability/instalment framing, or vice versa — to be read from the experiment, not assumed.
  • Balances above ₹25,000 convert at a different rate than smaller balances — untestable without a running-balance attribute; worth instrumenting if this matters strategically.
Worth settling before this is built
  • Entry can only filter on the Transaction entity (EMI Eligible=true, Settled). There is no way to also exclude, at entry, customers who already have an existing EMI Request (Pending, Failed, Cancelled, or Successful on a different balance). That means some customers who already started a conversion attempt — exactly the group you asked to exclude — will still receive these messages, e.g. someone whose request already failed or is sitting Pending will get 'convert your balance to EMI' as if they'd never tried. Do you want to accept this overlap for now, or hold the campaign until there's a way to check for an existing request at entry? This determines whether the campaign reaches people explicitly outside the intended audience, not just a targeting-precision shortfall. Until then: I will proceed with the overlap, relying on the automatic Goal Check to remove anyone who later reaches Successful, but Pending/Failed/Cancelled customers already in-flight would still be messaged.
Defaults applied
  • Wait durations between messages (48h after send 1, 72h after send 2). Shapes cadence and fatigue but has a sensible default under the stated 48h minimum-spacing constraint. Until then: Keep 48h / 72h spacing as proposed.
  • 10% control holdout, per tenant preference. Needed to read any directional effect against a no-contact baseline; without it only raw counts are available. Until then: Apply the tenant's stated 10% default.
Limitations
  • Transaction Events is marked new in the platform metadata: proposed, not confirmed as built in production. This campaign depends on it, so it cannot be presented as a verified platform capability.
  • EMI Events is marked new in the platform metadata: proposed, not confirmed as built in production. This campaign depends on it, so it cannot be presented as a verified platform capability.
  • Transaction Events and EMI Events are both marked 'new / proposed' in the platform metadata, not confirmed built in production. If either isn't actually live, this campaign cannot enter customers or detect its own goal.
Cannot be generated yet
  • steps[0].experiment.arms[0][1].condition: 2 open slots exist; the continuation is ambiguous.
  • steps[0].experiment.arms[1][1].condition: 2 open slots exist; the continuation is ambiguous.
Still unknown
  • Whether Transaction Events and EMI Events (both marked new/proposed, not confirmed built in production) are actually live — if not, this campaign cannot fire or measure its goal.
  • Whether the platform will ever expose a way to check for an existing EMI Request at entry, which would close the audience-overlap gap below.
Claims the journey does not support
  • Channel fallback was marked used, but no condition routes the failure path to a different channel, so delivery is attempted the same way either way.

You
We want to reactivate dormant credit cards. Customers who stopped transacting months ago. Design a drip campaign.
Agent
I've checked what events, attributes and channels this platform actually supports for a reactivation drip. Before designing I need three things settled, because each one points to a genuinely different campaign. First, 'dormant' can mean several different things in this data model — a customer with no recent customer-initiated transaction while the card is still live, versus an account the bank has already flagged Dormant, versus a card marked Inactive. These are different populations and different entry events, and the builder can only enter on one. Second, I have no business-owned definition yet of what 'working' looks like for this campaign — that has to come from you, not from me. Third, your own belief about why these customers stopped transacting (forgot the card exists, switched to a competitor, got stuck on a fee/limit concern, never properly activated it) points to different message mechanisms — a reminder, an incentive, or a friction fix — so I want your read before I pick one.
1What exactly should put a customer into this campaign — no customer-initiated transaction in some number of months while the card/account is still active, or the bank's own 'Dormant' account status / 'Inactive' card status? If it's the transaction-gap definition, roughly how many months of silence counts as dormant to you?
2How will you — the business — judge whether this campaign worked? For example, a share of entrants transacting again within some window, reactivation volume, something else you already track?
3What's your best guess at why these customers stopped transacting — forgot about the card, moved spend to a competitor card, a fee or limit concern, never really activated/used it from the start, or a mix? If you genuinely don't know, that's useful too — it tells me whether to test messages against each other rather than pick one.

On screenawaiting-confirmation208.9s
You
Dormant means no transaction in 6 months. Success is any transaction after we re-engage them. We think they've just forgotten about the card.
Agent
Re-engage card accounts the bank already classifies as Dormant with a short, low-cost-first message sequence that reminds customers the card is active and usable, testing the user's 'forgot about it' belief against a benefit-led alternative, with a held-out control group so any difference can be read as something more than noise. Success is read as any customer-initiated transaction after outreach, matched directly to a real Transaction event.
Approach
  • Entry on Account Status = 'Dormant' (tool: list_audience_attributes — this is the only buildable proxy for the user's 6-month no-transaction definition; no attribute reports transaction recency directly). Trade-off: this reaches the bank's own dormancy cohort, which may not align exactly with 'no transaction in 6 months' — it could be set on a different threshold or different criteria. This is flagged for the user to resolve, not assumed equivalent.
  • Goal on Transaction Events / Transaction, Initiated By = CUSTOMER_INITIATED, Transaction Status Any of [APPROVED, SETTLED] (tool: list_audience_attributes). This matches the user's own success definition ('any transaction') closely and excludes system-generated postings like fees or interest, which are not customer re-engagement.
  • Message mechanism is split into two experiment arms (reminder-led vs benefit-led) rather than committing to the single 'forgot the card' belief, because it is a user-belief with no supporting data and a real competing explanation exists (user-belief; own judgement on how to close it).
  • Channel order Email → SMS → WhatsApp, cheapest first, escalating cost only for customers who have not yet converted (tool: list_channels cost order; principle P-010). Trade-off: this is a cost/engagement heuristic, not validated for this bank.
  • 10% control group held out of the whole journey, per the tenant's stated preference for an explicit control on any campaign claiming incremental effect, and because no performance history exists for this bank to size an effect in advance (knowledge base; principle P-006).
Options weighed
  • Segmentation — not applicable here. No dimension surfaced (balance, utilisation, tenure) that the user believes should receive materially different treatment beyond the message-mechanism question, which is handled as an experiment, not a segment.
  • Experimentation — used. The believed cause (forgot the card) is untested; running reminder-led vs benefit-led copy, against a 10% control, lets the business read whether either mechanism moves transaction behaviour at all, and which one more, without claiming a number in advance.
  • Conditional branching — used. The platform auto-inserts a Goal Check and exit after every send/wait, so anyone who transacts leaves the journey immediately — this is the main branching point needed and it's built in.
  • Channel fallback — cannot evaluate yet. The builder has no fallback-channel field on a Send. The closest mechanism (a condition on the prior send's delivery outcome) would double the branches inside an already-2-armed experiment and push past a sensible message budget for a conservative, low-irritation campaign — not built here, disclosed as a limitation instead.
  • Adaptive sequencing — used. Channel escalates from Email to SMS to WhatsApp as the sequence progresses, reserving the higher-cost, more intrusive channel for the final nudge to whoever hasn't converted yet.
  • Cost and fatigue — used. Capped at 3 sends per arm (within the 4-message cap), spaced well beyond the 48-hour minimum. The weakest message is the final WhatsApp nudge — by that point two lower-cost touches have already failed to produce a transaction, so its incremental chance is probably the lowest of the three — kept because it is the last, low-absolute-cost chance before exit, not because it is expected to perform best.
  • Measurement and learning — used. Comparing the two arms against each other, and both against the 10% holdout, is the only way to separate 'the message worked' from 'they would have transacted anyway' — this campaign generates that evidence; it does not assume it in advance.
Considered and not used
  • Single-message blanket reminder with no experiment — Would commit the whole dormant population to one unverified mechanism (the 'forgot' belief) without any way to tell afterwards whether it was the right one, or whether anything happened beyond what would have happened anyway. Rejected in favour of the two-arm test plus control, which costs nothing extra in messages.
Success criteria
  • Business's own measure, as given: any transaction after the customer is re-engaged counts as success (user-owned definition).
Measurement
  • Track goal-completion rate (customer-initiated, approved/settled transaction) by experiment arm and against the 10% control holdout — this is the only way to separate a campaign effect from normal background reactivation.
  • Track delivery outcomes per channel (bounce/failure rates) to see whether Email is actually reaching this dormant population before concluding anything about message content.
  • A defined evaluation window (e.g., looking at transactions in the X days following entry) is needed to score this consistently — not yet given by the user, defaulted below.
  • No historical reactivation or lift figures exist for this bank; this campaign is the first data point, not a test against a known baseline.
Assumptions
  • Account Status = 'Dormant' is used as the entry population because it is the only live attribute resembling dormancy; it is not confirmed to equal 'no transaction in 6 months'.
  • A 60-day post-entry window is assumed for reading the success goal, aligned to roughly two statement cycles, in the absence of a stated window.
  • DNC and NPA exclusion are tenant-level hard constraints (knowledge base) and are assumed enforced by the platform's send infrastructure, since no DNC/NPA attribute is exposed in the audience model for us to filter on directly.
Hypotheses for future testing
  • A plain reminder that the card is active may recover some share of customers who simply forgot it exists (the user's stated belief).
  • A benefit-led message may outperform a plain reminder for customers whose dormancy is really about lapsed awareness of value, not forgetting — untested, to be read from the arm comparison.
Worth settling before this is built
  • The campaign can only enter customers on the bank's own Account Status = 'Dormant' flag, not on a literal 'no transaction in 6 months' calculation — no such field exists in this platform. Is the bank's 'Dormant' status flag set on that same 6-month transaction-gap logic, or something else (e.g. a longer regulatory threshold, or a different signal entirely)? If it's different, this campaign would reach a different population than the one described. If 'Dormant' status uses a longer or different threshold, the campaign would under- or over-reach the intended 6-month-silent population — someone could receive a reactivation message either much later than intended, or while still well within normal usage patterns. Until then: Proceeding with Account Status = 'Dormant' as the entry population, flagged to the user as a proxy, not a confirmed match.
  • Within accounts flagged Dormant, some cards may already be Inactive or blocked (the Account and Card entities can't be combined in one entry filter here). Are you comfortable that some entrants may be unable to transact even if the message lands, or should card-level usability be checked before building this? Messaging someone whose card is blocked asks them to do something they currently cannot do — that's a real experience cost, not just a wasted send. Until then: Proceeding on Account Status alone; recommend the campaign manager cross-check card usability outside this journey if that matters operationally.
Defaults applied
  • What time window should count a post-outreach transaction as attributable to this campaign (e.g. 30, 60, 90 days)? Changes only how the result is read, not who is targeted or what is sent. Until then: Defaulting to a 60-day evaluation window.
Limitations
  • Transaction Events is marked new in the platform metadata: proposed, not confirmed as built in production. This campaign depends on it, so it cannot be presented as a verified platform capability.
  • Transaction Events and Card Events are marked 'new — proposed, not confirmed built in production' by the platform. The goal (Transaction) and any card-level targeting depend on this being live. If Transaction Events aren't actually live yet, the goal check and therefore the whole measurement approach won't fire.
  • There is no fallback-channel field on a Send in this builder, so a failed Email cannot automatically retry on SMS within the same step. Some entrants with bad email addresses would simply not receive the first touch and wait out the gap before the SMS reminder arrives.

Dormant Card Reactivation — Reminder vs Benefit Test · control 10%

Re-engages credit card accounts flagged Dormant with a low-cost-first, capped message sequence, split into a reminder-led arm and a benefit-led arm against a held-out control, to test the business's 'customers forgot about the card' belief.

entry: {"kind": "audience", "entity": "Account", "conditions": [{"attribute": "Status", "operator": "Equals", "value": "Dormant"}]}
goal : {"eventCategory": "Transaction Events", "eventType": "Transaction", "conditions": [{"attribute": "Initiated By", "operator": "Equals", "value": "CUSTOMER_INITIATED"}, {"attribute": "Transaction Status", "operator": "Any of", "value": ["APPROVED", "SETTLED"]}]}
  1. EXPERIMENT
On screenawaiting-confirmation99.7s
You
Looks good.
Agent
Re-engage dormant card accounts with a short, low-cost-first message sequence, testing the business's 'forgot about it' belief against a benefit-led alternative, with a 10% control held out so any difference can be read as more than background noise. Success is any customer-initiated, approved/settled transaction after outreach, matched to a real Transaction event.
Approach
  • Entry on Account Status = 'Dormant' (tool: list_audience_attributes — confirmed allowed value) — the only buildable proxy for the user's 6-month no-transaction definition; no attribute reports transaction recency. Trade-off flagged as q2-0, not assumed equivalent.
  • Goal on Transaction Events / Transaction, Initiated By = CUSTOMER_INITIATED, Transaction Status Any of [APPROVED, SETTLED] (tool: list_audience_attributes, confirmed allowed values) — matches the user's 'any transaction' success definition and excludes system-generated postings like fees/interest.
  • Two experiment arms (reminder-led vs benefit-led copy) rather than committing to the single 'forgot the card' belief, because it is user-belief with no supporting data and a real competing explanation (lapsed benefit awareness) exists — own judgement on how to close it, given the user approved proceeding without separating the two explanations themselves.
  • Channel order Email → SMS → WhatsApp, cheapest first (tool: list_channels, confirmed cost order), escalating only for customers who have not yet converted — each send's prior goal check auto-exits anyone who already transacted (platform behaviour, P-008).
  • 10% control group held out of the whole journey (tenant preference, knowledge base) because no performance history exists for this bank to size an effect in advance (P-006); without it, any observed reactivation cannot be separated from what would have happened anyway.
Options weighed
  • Segmentation — not applicable here. No dimension surfaced (balance, tenure, utilisation) that the user believes warrants a different treatment beyond message mechanism, which is handled as an experiment, not a segment.
  • Experimentation — used. The believed cause ('forgot the card') is untested; reminder-led vs benefit-led arms against a 10% control let the business read whether either mechanism moves transaction behaviour, without claiming a number in advance.
  • Conditional branching — used. The platform auto-inserts a Goal Check and exit after every send/wait (P-008); anyone who transacts leaves immediately — the main branch needed is built in.
  • Channel fallback — not applicable here. The builder has no fallback-channel field on a Send (confirmed by list_step_types/builder capability notes); a condition on delivery outcome would double branches inside an already 2-armed experiment, which is disproportionate for a 3-message-per-arm sequence. Disclosed as a limitation instead.
  • Adaptive sequencing — used. Channel escalates Email → SMS → WhatsApp as the sequence ages, reserving the higher-cost, more intrusive channel for the final nudge to whoever hasn't converted yet (P-010).
  • Cost and fatigue — used. 3 sends per arm (within the 4-message cap), spaced well beyond the 48-hour minimum. The weakest message is the final WhatsApp nudge — by then two cheaper touches have already failed to produce a transaction — kept because it is the last, low-absolute-cost chance before exit, not because it is expected to outperform.
  • Measurement and learning — used. Comparing the two arms against each other, and both against the 10% holdout, is the only way to separate 'the message worked' from 'they would have transacted anyway' (P-006) — this campaign generates that evidence rather than assuming it.
Considered and not used
  • Single-message blanket reminder with no experiment — Would commit the whole dormant population to one unverified mechanism (the 'forgot' belief) with no way to tell afterwards whether it was right, or whether anything happened beyond background reactivation. The two-arm test plus control costs nothing extra in message volume.
Success criteria
  • Business's own measure, as given: any customer transaction after re-engagement counts as success.
Measurement
  • Goal-completion rate (customer-initiated, approved/settled transaction) by experiment arm, read against the 10% control holdout — the only way to separate a campaign effect from normal background reactivation.
  • Delivery outcomes per channel (e.g. hard bounce on Email, failed-DND on SMS — tool: list_channels delivery statuses) to check reach before concluding anything about message content.
  • A defined post-entry evaluation window is needed to score this consistently; defaulted to 60 days in the absence of a stated window (optional-preference, see openItems).
  • No historical reactivation or lift figures exist for this bank (knowledge base) — this campaign is a first data point, not a test against a known baseline.
Assumptions
  • Account Status = 'Dormant' is used as the entry population because it is the only attribute resembling dormancy; not confirmed to equal 'no transaction in 6 months' (carried as q2-0).
  • A 60-day post-entry window is assumed for reading the success goal in the absence of a stated window.
  • DNC and NPA exclusion are tenant-level hard constraints (knowledge base) assumed enforced by the platform's send infrastructure, since no DNC/NPA attribute is exposed in the audience model to filter on directly.
Hypotheses for future testing
  • A plain reminder that the card is active may recover some share of customers who simply forgot it exists (the user's stated belief).
  • A benefit-led message may outperform a plain reminder for customers whose dormancy is really about lapsed awareness of value, not forgetting — untested, to be read from the arm comparison.
Defaults applied
  • What time window should count a post-outreach transaction as attributable to this campaign for reading results (e.g. 30, 60, 90 days)? Changes only how the result is read, not who is targeted or what is sent. Until then: Defaulting to a 60-day evaluation window.
Limitations
  • Transaction Events is marked new in the platform metadata: proposed, not confirmed as built in production. This campaign depends on it, so it cannot be presented as a verified platform capability.
  • Transaction Events (the goal) and Card Events are marked 'new — proposed, not confirmed built in production' by the platform metadata. If Transaction Events are not actually live, the goal check — and therefore the entire measurement approach and auto-exit-on-conversion behaviour — will not fire.
  • There is no fallback-channel field on a Send in this builder, so a failed Email cannot automatically retry on SMS within the same step. Entrants with bad email addresses simply miss the first touch and wait out the gap until the scheduled SMS reminder, rather than getting an immediate recovery message.

You
I want to increase OS-to-EMI conversions. Design a drip campaign for this.
Agent
The platform does confirm the product: EMI Request carries a Source value of 'OS-to-EMI' and an EMI_STATUS_CHANGED event with statuses Pending/Successful/Failed/Expired/Cancelled, so I can build on that. But before designing I need three things only the business can give me: how success will be judged, which customer behaviour we're actually trying to change (two materially different populations are plausible here), and what you believe is stopping conversion today, since that drives the message content. Getting these wrong means building the wrong campaign, not just a weaker one.
1How should we judge whether this campaign is working — e.g. number of OS-to-EMI requests initiated, requests completed successfully (EMI Request status = Successful), or something else like total outstanding balance converted? This is your call, not a platform default.
2Who is the target: (a) customers carrying an outstanding balance who are eligible for EMI but have never started a conversion request, or (b) customers who already started an OS-to-EMI request (status Pending) but did not complete it before it expired? These are different audiences needing different entry points and messages — or do you want both as separate journeys?
3What do you believe is actually stopping customers from converting — not understanding the EMI option exists, hesitating over interest cost/total payable, finding the in-app process confusing, or something else? If you're not sure, say so and we can treat it as an open question rather than guess.

These sit at different points in the sequence, need different entry events (eligibility signal vs EMI Request Pending), and probably different copy. A wrong guess here aims the campaign at the wrong people entirely.
  • opennone Believed cause of non-conversion
    why Awareness, cost/interest hesitation, process friction and commitment hesitation each point to a different message (educate, reassure on cost, simplify steps, reduce perceived lock-in). This is a belief only the business can offer, and it should not be designed around silently.
  • opennone Outstanding balance size / segment
    why Whether high-balance and low-balance revolvers deserve different treatment (e.g. bigger potential EMI saving framing vs light-touch nudge) could change segmentation, but may not be essential to a first version.

You
Option (a) — customers who are eligible but have never started a conversion request.
Agent
Target customers with an EMI-eligible outstanding transaction who have never initiated an OS-to-EMI request, and nudge them toward starting and completing one, measured by EMI Requests reaching Successful. The opening message leads with cost transparency and a fixed, predictable payment (the user's hypothesised barrier), with a recovery path on delivery failure and a later reminder that leans on statement-cycle urgency qualitatively, since per-customer due-date timing cannot be wired into this entry signal.
Approach
  • Goal = EMI_STATUS_CHANGED with New Status = Successful — directly reflects the user's own success definition (basis: user).
  • Entry = Transaction event with EMI Eligible = true and Transaction Status Any of [APPROVED, SETTLED] — this is the closest buildable proxy for 'an eligible outstanding balance exists' (basis: tool, for what the attribute actually means; judgement, for using it as the opportunity signal).
  • No entry filter excludes customers who already have a Pending, Failed or Cancelled EMI request — entry conditions are scoped to the Transaction entity only, and EMI Request is a different entity. Customers who reach Successful are auto-excluded by the platform's goal check, but those mid-request or previously declined are not. This is disclosed below as a strategic ambiguity, not swept under 'operational limitation', because it changes who actually receives the 'you haven't started yet' framing (basis: tool constraint + judgement on its consequence).
  • No balance-size or due-date filter is applied at entry, for the reasons in the 'Outstanding balance size / segment' dimension — the hypothesis is carried, not built (basis: tool + user-belief).
  • Message content leads generically with total-cost transparency and a fixed EMI amount rather than naming a specific cost lever, because narrowing the 'interest-cost hesitation' belief further would not change the first message (basis: judgement, deferred per the dimension note).
  • Channel sequence leads with EMAIL (lowest cost) and reserves SMS/WHATSAPP for the delivery-failure recovery path and later reinforcement, per the tenant's stated preference to lead with the cheaper channel (basis: tenant preference, knowledge base P-010).
  • Sequence length and spacing respect the 4-message cap and 48-hour minimum spacing in every path, including the delivery-failure recovery branch (basis: tool/knowledge-base constraint).
Options weighed
  • Segmentation — not applicable here. The two segmentation hunches the user raised (balance size, due-date proximity) cannot be built as real segments with today's attributes; see dimensions. No other segmenting factor was raised, so one treatment for all eligible non-starters is used, with the caveat above.
  • Experimentation — cannot evaluate yet. A real competing hypothesis exists (e.g. 'lead with fixed-EMI amount' vs 'lead with total interest saved'), and P-005/P-006 support testing it with a holdout. I have not built an A/B arm here because the user has not indicated which specific cost framings they want compared — recommend as a next step once copy variants are agreed, not fabricated now.
  • Conditional branching — used. Branches on the first send's delivery outcome (DELIVERED vs not) to recover non-delivered customers via a different channel rather than losing them silently.
  • Channel fallback — used. True per-send fallback isn't buildable here (platform limitation), so it is expressed as a condition-on-delivery-outcome step routing to an SMS resend — the closest supported equivalent.
  • Adaptive sequencing — used. The final message shifts tone to statement-cycle urgency as the journey ages, even though it cannot be timed to each customer's actual due date — a qualitative adaptation, not a precise one.
  • Cost and fatigue — used. Capped at 3 messages for the normal path and 4 for the recovery path (the cap), spaced 48h+ apart. The weakest message is the final WhatsApp urgency reminder — it carries the least new information, repeating the offer with a cycle-urgency frame — but it is kept because it is the only touch that attempts timing-based relevance at all, and it is the lowest-frequency, last-resort send.
  • Measurement and learning — used. Track EMI Requests reaching Successful among entrants, against the 10% control group the tenant prefers. Without that holdout this can only report what happened, not what the campaign caused (P-006).
Considered and not used
  • Running this as a one-off broadcast instead of a drip — A single message cannot both recover non-deliveries and layer in a later urgency reminder; the user's own hypotheses (cost hesitation, due-date urgency) call for at least an opening message and a differently-framed follow-up, which needs a sequence.
Success criteria
  • More EMI Requests reaching New Status = Successful among the entered audience — no fixed numeric target, per the user.
Measurement
  • Track EMI_STATUS_CHANGED volumes by New Status (Pending, Successful, Failed, Expired, Cancelled) for entrants vs the control group.
  • Track delivery outcomes per channel per step to see how often the recovery branch fires.
  • To measure properly: compare Successful-rate for the treatment group against the 10% holdout over the same window; without that comparison, only raw counts can be reported, not any lift (P-006).
Assumptions
  • DNC suppression, NPA exclusion and quiet-hours enforcement are applied automatically by the platform as tenant-wide guardrails, not as conditions this blueprint needs to encode.
  • Transaction Events and EMI Events are marked 'new-proposed' in platform metadata — this design assumes they will be live; if not yet built, neither entry nor goal can fire.
Hypotheses for future testing
  • Leading with total-cost transparency and a fixed EMI amount will reduce cost-hesitation drop-off more than a generic 'convert now' message — untested.
  • A reminder framed around the statement cycle will prompt action better than a flat time-based reminder — untested, and currently only approximated since per-customer due-date timing isn't wired into this entry signal.
Worth settling before this is built
  • Customers who already have a Pending, Failed or Cancelled OS-to-EMI request (i.e. did start, just not successfully) will still enter this 'never started' campaign and receive 'you can convert your balance' messaging, because entry conditions can't exclude them (different entity from the Transaction trigger). Is that acceptable, or should those customers be excluded — which would need a separate mechanism outside this blueprint? If unacceptable, it changes who should receive this campaign and likely needs a second journey or a pre-filter outside this tool. Until then: Will proceed as designed: only customers who reach Successful are auto-excluded (via the platform's goal check); others mid-process or previously declined will still receive first-touch messaging.
Defaults applied
  • Should a true A/B test of cost-framing (fixed-EMI-amount vs total-interest-saved) be set up once copy direction is agreed? Would let the bank learn which cost lever actually drives conversion, rather than guessing generically. Until then: Default: ship the generic cost-transparency framing as a single arm for now; revisit as a follow-up experiment.
Limitations
  • Transaction Events is marked new in the platform metadata: proposed, not confirmed as built in production. This campaign depends on it, so it cannot be presented as a verified platform capability.
  • EMI Events is marked new in the platform metadata: proposed, not confirmed as built in production. This campaign depends on it, so it cannot be presented as a verified platform capability.
  • Targeting by outstanding balance size (e.g. above ₹25,000) and by proximity to statement due date cannot be built as entry filters — no running-balance attribute exists, and Statement Due Date sits on a different entity than the Transaction-based entry signal. The campaign cannot test or act on either of the user's two segmentation hunches; messaging is uniform across balance sizes and due-date timing.

The objective is reactivating dormant credit cards, but three things would each lead to a materially different campaign. First, 'stopped transacting months ago' could mean different recency windows, and the platform exposes Account Status = Dormant as a ready-made flag that may or may not match what you mean by dormant — if it doesn't, we'd need to build audience logic around a transaction-recency signal instead, which is a different (and currently 'new-proposed', unconfirmed) event category. Second, you haven't told me how you'd judge this working, which the brief requires me to ask before designing rather than assume. Third, why these customers went quiet changes the message entirely: a lapsed-rewards story, a 'we miss you' nudge, and a friction fix (e.g. a card that's actually blocked or expired) are different campaigns, not variations of one. I checked the platform's event/attribute catalogue and channels before asking, so these three are genuinely open, not things a tool can answer for me.

3What's your best guess at why these customers stopped transacting — e.g. the card lost its appeal/rewards, they now primarily use a different card, something is blocking the card itself (expired/locked), or they simply forgot about it? You
Dormant means no transaction in 6 months. Success is any transaction after we re-engage them. We think they've just forgotten about the card.
Agent
Re-engage customers whose account is flagged Dormant with a short, low-pressure reminder sequence that leads with the lower-cost channel and escalates only if needed, on the hypothesis that they simply forgot the card exists. A 10% holdout lets the business read incremental effect, and a message-angle test (plain reminder vs benefit-led reminder) gives evidence on whether 'forgot' is the right framing, not just the right belief.
Approach
  • Entry = Account.Status Equals 'Dormant' (tool: list_audience_attributes). This is the only buildable proxy for 'no transaction in 6 months' — the user's own threshold is not independently verifiable against this flag's internal definition.
  • Goal = Transaction event with Transaction Status Any of [APPROVED, SETTLED] (tool: list_event_types/list_audience_attributes). Chosen to match the user's 'any transaction' success definition while excluding non-completed states like a reversed or expired attempt; this is my refinement of their wording, not something they specified, so it's an assumption.
  • Message angle A/B at first touch (my recommendation, nothing confirmed): tests the user's 'forgot' belief against a benefit-led alternative, since the belief was given as a guess, not a finding.
  • Lower-cost-first channel order, Email then SMS then WhatsApp (tenant preference: 'prefer lower-cost channel first', tool: list_channels cost order) — WhatsApp (highest cost) reserved for the final reinforcement touch.
  • 10% control group (tenant preference stated in brief) so any observed transaction uptick can be compared against a held-out group rather than asserted as caused by the campaign.
Options weighed
  • Segmentation — used. Dormant accounts whose card is actually blocked/locked need a service fix, not a reminder — recommended as a distinct treatment, though the entry step can only filter one entity so this split is not buildable today (see open item).
  • Experimentation — used. A/B the first-touch message angle (plain reminder vs benefit-led) to get directional evidence on the stated 'forgot' belief, without adding message volume.
  • Conditional branching — used. Branch on the first email's delivery outcome: if it failed to deliver, move to SMS immediately rather than waiting out the normal reminder spacing for a message that never arrived.
  • Channel fallback — cannot evaluate yet. True per-send fallback (same message, alternate channel, same step) is not a field this blueprint can set. Approximated with the delivery-outcome condition above; that is a journey-level workaround, not the real feature — flagged as a limitation.
  • Adaptive sequencing — used. Sequence escalates from cheapest (Email) to costliest (WhatsApp) as the opportunity ages, per the tenant's stated cost-ordering preference.
  • Cost and fatigue — used. Capped at 3 sends (within the 4-message cap), each ≥48h apart. Weakest message is the final WhatsApp reinforcement — by that point the customer has had two chances to act, and WhatsApp is the costliest channel; kept as the one last-chance touch, but it's the first one I'd cut if fatigue becomes a concern.
  • Measurement and learning — used. 10% control group gives an incremental read of the whole campaign; the message-angle A/B separately gives a directional read on cause. Neither produces a performance number today — no history exists for this bank.
Considered and not used
  • A non-messaging intervention (e.g. outbound call or a bonus/cashback incentive offer) as the primary mechanism — The brief asks for a drip campaign and gives no incentive budget or mandate; a messaging-only reminder matches the stated 'forgot' hypothesis. If the message-angle test or the blocked/locked segment finding later shows 'forgot' is wrong for a meaningful slice, an incentive or a service-fix track (not more messages) would be the better next move.
Success criteria
  • Business's own measure (their words): any transaction after re-engagement counts as success — no minimum amount or count specified.
Measurement
  • Track, per arm (benefit-led vs plain reminder) and vs the 10% control: delivery rate per channel, and rate of a completed (APPROVED/SETTLED) transaction in the period following first message receipt.
  • Read the control-vs-treatment gap as the only defensible signal of incremental effect; read the arm-vs-arm gap as directional evidence on message angle, not a confirmed lift.
  • To measure properly would need: a defined attribution window (not specified by the user — e.g. 30/60/90 days post-send), and confirmation that the Transaction Events category is actually live in production (currently marked new-proposed).
Assumptions
  • Account.Status = 'Dormant' is treated as the operative entry condition since no direct 'days since last transaction' attribute exists for audience filtering.
  • A completed transaction (APPROVED or SETTLED) is treated as 'a transaction' for the goal; a reversed, expired or cancelled one is not.
  • DNC and NPA exclusion and quiet-hours (21:00–09:00) are enforced by the platform automatically, per the stated hard constraints.
  • Generic 'your card and its benefits' language is used since no specific, currently-valid benefit/reward claim was supplied.
Hypotheses for future testing
  • If customers mainly forgot the card exists, a benefit-led reminder will show a higher transaction-after-message rate than a plain 'you haven't used this' reminder — worth testing, not assumed.
  • Customers whose card is blocked or locked will not respond to any reminder message, regardless of angle — worth checking once/if blocked-card exclusion is buildable.
Worth settling before this is built
  • You defined dormant as 'no transaction in 6 months.' The only buildable entry condition is the system flag Account.Status = 'Dormant', whose own threshold is not confirmed to be 180 days — it could be shorter, longer, or based on a different rule entirely. Do you want to proceed on this flag as-is, or do you need the 6-month threshold built and verified before this campaign reaches anyone? If the flag's threshold differs from your 6 months, the campaign will reach a different population than you intended — either messaging people too soon or missing people who've genuinely gone quiet. Until then: Proceed using Account.Status = 'Dormant' as the entry condition, flagged to you as an approximation, not a confirmed match to '6 months.'
  • The entry step can only filter on one entity's attributes, so we cannot combine 'Account.Status = Dormant' with 'Card is not blocked/locked' in the same audience. That means some customers who get this 'come back and use your card' message will have a card they physically cannot use. Do you want to accept that overlap for now, or hold this campaign until blocked/locked exclusion can be built? Sending a reactivation nudge to someone whose card is blocked is not a minor miss — it reaches the wrong customer with a message that cannot apply to them, and may prompt a complaint or a support contact instead of a transaction. Until then: Launch without the exclusion (platform limitation), and recommend a manual check of block/lock status against the dormant list outside this tool before each send, until the capability exists.
Defaults applied
  • No specific, currently-valid card benefit or reward was supplied for the benefit-led message variant. Overly specific but inaccurate benefit claims would misrepresent the card. Until then: Default to generic, non-specific 'your card and its benefits' language rather than naming a reward.
Limitations
  • Transaction Events is marked new in the platform metadata: proposed, not confirmed as built in production. This campaign depends on it, so it cannot be presented as a verified platform capability.
  • Transaction Events (the goal event) is marked 'new-proposed' in this platform's metadata, not confirmed built in production. If this event isn't actually live, the goal can't fire and the automatic goal-check/exit behaviour won't work, so converters would keep receiving messages.
  • A true per-send channel fallback (same message, alternate channel, same step) is not a field this blueprint can set. Delivery failures on the first channel won't automatically retry on another within the same step.

  1. EXPERIMENT
On screenawaiting-confirmation132.4s
You
Looks good. Keep the messages friendly in tone.
Agent
Re-engage customers whose account carries the Dormant flag with a short, friendly, low-pressure sequence that leads with the cheapest channel and escalates only if needed. The first message is A/B tested between a plain reminder and a benefit-led reminder to get directional evidence on the user's 'they forgot' belief, rather than assuming it. A 10% holdout lets the business read whether any uptick in transactions is more than what would have happened anyway.
Approach
  • Entry = Account.Status Equals 'Dormant' — decision rests on tool (list_audience_attributes confirms 'Dormant' is an allowed value); trade-off: this is a proxy for the user's stated 6-month no-transaction definition, not a verified match to it (carried as q2-0).
  • Goal = Transaction event, Transaction Status Any of [APPROVED, SETTLED] — rests on tool (list_audience_attributes allowed values) plus the user's own success definition ('any transaction'); my refinement is excluding EXPIRED/CANCELED/PARTIALLY_SETTLED so an incomplete attempt isn't falsely counted — this narrowing is my judgement, not something the user specified.
  • Message-angle experiment at first touch — my recommendation, nothing confirmed by the user — tests the 'forgot' belief (user-belief) against a benefit-led alternative rather than designing silently for one reading.
  • Lower-cost-channel-first ordering (Email → SMS → WhatsApp) — rests on tenant preference ('prefer lower-cost channel first') and tool (list_channels cost order).
  • Delivery-outcome condition after the first send, approximating channel fallback — rests on platform constraint (true per-send fallback is not buildable per the builder capability list); trade-off stated as a limitation below.
  • 10% control group — rests on tenant stated preference ('preferred control group % = 10') so any observed effect can be read against a holdout rather than asserted as caused.
Options weighed
  • Segmentation — cannot evaluate yet. A blocked/locked-card segment deserves a different treatment (service fix, not a usage nudge) but the entry step filters only one entity's attributes, so Account.Status and Card.Locked/Blocked cannot be combined today (q2-1). Would need either a combined-entity filter or a pre-built segment to decide the split.
  • Experimentation — used. A/B the first-touch message angle (plain vs benefit-led) to get directional evidence on the stated 'forgot' belief, which is otherwise untested.
  • Conditional branching — used. Branch on the first send's delivery outcome: if the email never delivered, the SMS reminder is framed as a first contact, not a follow-up to something they already saw.
  • Channel fallback — cannot evaluate yet. True per-send fallback (same message, alternate channel, same step) is not a field this blueprint can set. Approximated with a delivery-outcome condition one step later, which is a journey-level workaround, not the real feature.
  • Adaptive sequencing — used. Sequence escalates from cheapest (Email) to costliest (WhatsApp) as the opportunity ages, per tenant cost-ordering preference, and the final touch is reserved for customers who haven't yet converted or unsubscribed via the auto-inserted goal check.
  • Cost and fatigue — used. Capped at 3 sends per path (within the 4-message cap), each spaced ≥48h. Weakest message is the final WhatsApp reinforcement — by then the customer has had two prior chances and WhatsApp is the costliest channel; kept as a single last-chance touch, but the first one to cut if fatigue becomes a concern.
  • Measurement and learning — used. 10% control gives an incremental read of the whole campaign; the message-angle split gives a directional read on the 'forgot' belief. Neither produces a performance number today — no history exists for this bank (per knowledge base).
Considered and not used
  • A non-messaging intervention (outbound call, bonus/cashback offer) as the primary mechanism — The brief asks for a drip campaign and specifies no incentive budget or mandate; a messaging-only reminder matches the stated 'forgot' hypothesis. If the message-angle test or a future blocked/locked finding shows 'forgot' is wrong for a meaningful slice, an incentive or a service-fix track would be the better next move, not more messages.
Success criteria
  • Business's own measure (their words): any transaction at all after re-engagement counts as success — no minimum amount or count specified.
Measurement
  • Track, per message-angle arm and vs the 10% control: delivery rate per channel, and rate of a completed (APPROVED/SETTLED) transaction following first message receipt.
  • Read the control-vs-treatment gap as the only defensible signal of incremental effect; read the arm-vs-arm gap as directional evidence on message angle, not a confirmed lift.
  • To measure properly would need: a defined attribution window (not specified by the user), and confirmation that Transaction Events is actually live in production (currently marked new-proposed in platform metadata).
Assumptions
  • Account.Status = 'Dormant' is treated as the operative entry condition since no direct 'days since last transaction' attribute exists for audience filtering.
  • A completed transaction (APPROVED or SETTLED) is treated as 'a transaction' for the goal; a reversed, expired or cancelled one is not.
  • DNC, NPA exclusion and quiet-hours (21:00–09:00) are enforced by the platform automatically, per the stated hard constraints.
  • Generic 'your card and its benefits' language is used in the benefit-led arm since no specific, currently-valid reward claim was supplied.
Hypotheses for future testing
  • If customers mainly forgot the card exists, a benefit-led reminder will show a higher post-message transaction rate than a plain reminder — worth testing, not assumed.
  • Customers whose card is blocked or locked will not respond to any reminder message regardless of angle — worth checking once/if blocked-card exclusion is buildable.
Defaults applied
  • No specific, currently-valid card benefit or reward was supplied for the benefit-led message variant. Naming a specific, inaccurate benefit would misrepresent the card. Until then: Default to generic, non-specific 'your card and its benefits' language rather than naming a reward.
Limitations
  • Transaction Events is marked new in the platform metadata: proposed, not confirmed as built in production. This campaign depends on it, so it cannot be presented as a verified platform capability.
  • Transaction Events (the goal event) is marked 'new-proposed' in platform metadata, not confirmed built in production. If this event isn't actually live, the goal can't fire, the automatic goal-check/exit won't trigger, and converters would keep receiving messages after they've already succeeded.
  • A true per-send channel fallback (same message, alternate channel, same step) is not a field this blueprint can set. Delivery failures on the first channel don't automatically retry within the same step; the condition-based workaround only reacts one step later.
Cannot be generated yet

  • steps[0].experiment.arms[0][2].condition: 2 open slots exist; the continuation is ambiguous.
  • steps[0].experiment.arms[1][1].wait: 2 open slots exist; the continuation is ambiguous.
  • steps[0].experiment.arms[1][2].condition: 2 open slots exist; the continuation is ambiguous.
Still unknown
  • Whether Account.Status = 'Dormant' actually triggers at 6 months or some other threshold (q2-0, carried).
  • What proportion of Dormant accounts have a blocked or locked card, who should probably not receive a usage nudge (q2-1, carried).
  • The true mix of root causes behind dormancy beyond the stated 'forgot' belief — the experiment gives directional evidence, not a definitive answer.

Dormant Card Reactivation — Friendly Reminder · control 10%

Reactivation drip for accounts flagged Dormant. Tests a plain vs benefit-led opening message, escalates from Email to SMS to WhatsApp, and holds out 10% as a control.

entry: {"kind": "audience", "entity": "Account", "conditions": [{"attribute": "Status", "operator": "Equals", "value": "Dormant"}]}
goal : {"eventCategory": "Transaction Events", "eventType": "Transaction", "conditions": [{"attribute": "Transaction Status", "operator": "Any of", "value": ["APPROVED", "SETTLED"]}]}
  1. EXPERIMENT

e2e archived

3 turns 332s total 2026-10-15 10:13

This run was recorded before turn records were kept, so it cannot show which prompt blocks applied. The transcript is unchanged.

On screendiscovery45.4s
You
I want to increase OS-to-EMI conversions. Design a drip campaign for this.
Agent
I checked the platform vocabulary and found a concrete match: EMI Request has a Source value literally called 'OS-to-EMI' (alongside Txn-to-EMI, Multi-Txn-to-EMI, Onboarding, Card Activation), with a New Status of Pending/Successful/Failed/Expired/Cancelled. That confirms 'OS-to-EMI' means converting an existing outstanding card balance into an EMI plan, and gives a real goal event (New Status = Successful, Source = OS-to-EMI). But the vocabulary has no event for 'customer now has an outstanding balance eligible for conversion' — the only OS-to-EMI signal fires once a request already exists (Pending/Failed/Expired). That is a real fork: am I building an acquisition campaign (reach customers who haven't started a conversion at all) or a recovery campaign (reach customers whose OS-to-EMI request stalled before completing)? Those need different entry points, different audiences and different messages, so I need this settled before designing. I also need the business's own success measure, which only the user can give, and their belief about why customers aren't converting, since that belief determines what the messages should say (and competing explanations imply different copy).
1How will you judge whether this campaign is working — what's the business measure of success (e.g. number of OS-to-EMI conversions per month, conversion rate among those who see the offer, reduction in revolving balances, something else)? If you don't have a target yet, say so and I'll record it as still open.
2Are we primarily trying to reach customers who have an outstanding balance but have never started an OS-to-EMI conversion (pure acquisition), or customers who started a conversion request that went Pending/Failed/Expired without completing (recovery of a stalled request) — or both, as separate tracks?
3What's your working theory for why eligible customers aren't converting — do you think it's mostly unawareness that the option exists, hesitation about the interest/fees, or drop-off partway through the request flow? (If you genuinely don't know, I'll treat the reasons as competing and keep messaging generic rather than guessing.)
Not on screen — what the application recorded
Dimension record
  • opennone Funnel stage targeted (never-started vs stalled OS-to-EMI request)
    why The only usable entry signals sit at different points in the funnel — there is no event for 'balance became eligible', only for a request that already exists (Pending/Failed/Expired) or completed (Successful). Which population is meant changes the entry event, the audience, and the message entirely.
  • opennone Believed driver of non-conversion (awareness vs cost concern vs flow drop-off)
    why Different causes call for different message content — an awareness message, a cost/benefit-reframing message, and a 'finish what you started' nudge are not interchangeable. This is the user's belief about their own customers, not something I can look up.
  • opennone Customer/balance segmentation (who these customers are, size of outstanding balance)
    why Whether high-balance or specific customer segments deserve different treatment could change whether this is one uniform journey or several, but I don't yet know if the user believes this matters enough to split the audience.
Success criteria

Empty — not settled at this point in the conversation.
