On screenawaiting-confirmation233.0s
You
Success is simply more of these cards transacting again. Dormant means no transaction in 6 months. We think they've just forgotten about the card.
Agent
A reminder-led drip for cardholders whose account is flagged Dormant, built on the user's own hypothesis that they simply forgot the card exists. Three low-to-high-cost touches (email, SMS, WhatsApp) nudge them to transact again, with a delivery-outcome branch acting as channel recovery, and a 10% holdout so any observed difference can be read against a baseline rather than claimed as caused.
Approach
  • Audience = Account.Status Equals 'Dormant' (tool: list_audience_attributes). This is the closest built-in proxy to the user's '6 months no transaction' definition, not the definition itself — flagged as a gap below, not silently substituted.
  • Single uniform message track, no segmentation by cause or value tier (user: stated one cause, no sub-groups; tool: no value/limit attribute exists to segment on even if it mattered).
  • Goal = a customer-initiated, approved/settled card authorization (Transaction Events category) — the closest available proof that the card is 'transacting again' (tool: list_audience_attributes, list_event_types). This category is marked new-proposed, not confirmed live in production (tool).
  • Lead with EMAIL (cheapest), reserve SMS/WhatsApp for reinforcement, per tenant preference to prefer lower-cost channel first (brief: channel cost order; P-010 hypothesis).
  • 10% control group held out, per tenant's stated preference and P-006 (a lift claim needs a holdout) — this is my recommendation applying their stated preference, not something they asked for in this conversation.
  • Delivery-outcome condition after the first send doubles as channel-fallback logic, since the builder has no per-send fallback field (tool: list_step_types / stated platform limitation) — built as an explicit branch instead.
Options weighed
  • Segmentation — not applicable here. User's working theory is a single uniform cause (forgetting) with no named sub-groups; one treatment for the whole dormant base matches what they told us. Value/risk tiering is a real open question but unresolved and unbuildable today — kept as a limitation, not folded into this version.
  • Experimentation — used. 10% holdout lets the team compare reactivation among entrants vs non-entrants, which is the minimum needed to separate a campaign effect from customers who would have come back anyway (P-006).
  • Conditional branching — used. Branches on the first send's delivery outcome: if the email didn't deliver, the next touch resends the core message on SMS instead of assuming it was seen; if it delivered, SMS reinforces instead.
  • Channel fallback — used. True per-send fallback isn't buildable here (platform limitation); implemented as the closest supported equivalent, a condition on the prior send's delivery outcome that re-routes the next message's content and channel.
  • Adaptive sequencing — not applicable here. Dormancy here has no hard expiry or ageing deadline (unlike, say, an EMI offer), so there's no natural urgency curve to escalate against. Cadence stays flat: three evenly spaced reminders.
  • Cost and fatigue — used. Capped at 3 sends (within the 4-message ceiling), each 48h apart, cheapest channel first. The weakest message is the final WhatsApp touch — two channels have already tried to reach the customer by then — but it's kept because WhatsApp read-rates are typically different from email/SMS, so it's a distinct chance rather than pure repetition; if it proves ineffective later, it's the first candidate to cut.
  • Measurement and learning — used. Holdout vs entrants gives a descriptive comparison. Without randomising message content itself, this tells us whether the campaign coincides with more reactivation, not which message mechanism caused it — stated as a limit, not a result.
Considered and not used
  • An incentive-led reactivation offer (e.g. bonus cashback or a fee waiver for the next transaction) instead of a plain reminder — The user's own theory is simple forgetting, not disengagement from lack of value, and no incentive or budget was confirmed. Testing the cheaper, no-cost reminder hypothesis first fits the bank's stated conservative risk appetite; an incentive track is a reasonable next experiment if plain reminders show no movement, not a reason to hold this one back.
Success criteria
  • More dormant-card accounts recording a transaction after the campaign than would be expected without it — the business's own measure, judged qualitatively by the team, not a numeric target.
Measurement
  • Track the share of entrants with a customer-initiated approved/settled transaction after entry, compared with the 10% holdout over the same window — this is the only comparison available to separate campaign effect from customers who'd have come back anyway.
  • Track delivery and engagement (opened/clicked/read where the channel reports it) per send to see which touch coincides with reactivation, acknowledging this is correlational, not causal.
  • No historical performance data exists for this bank (verified in the knowledge base), so there is no baseline rate to compare against yet — early reads should be treated as descriptive until volume accumulates.
  • A cleaner read of WHICH message mechanism (reminder tone vs benefit-led vs incentive) actually moves people would need a randomised content test, which this campaign does not run — noted as a hypothesis for a future, separate experiment.
Assumptions
  • DNC and NPA exclusion (both required per the tenant's hard constraints) are assumed to be enforced by the platform at send time as global suppression, since no explicit DNC/NPA attribute is exposed to filter on in the audience builder; this campaign does not separately encode them.
  • Account.Status='Dormant' is assumed to be a reasonable stand-in for 'no transaction in 6 months' for this proposal, pending confirmation that the bank's own Dormant-flag threshold matches 6 months.
Hypotheses for future testing
  • Many dormant cardholders simply forgot the card exists; restoring visibility of it and its benefits through a low-friction reminder is enough to prompt a repeat transaction, without needing a monetary incentive.
Worth settling before this is built
  • Should high-value or higher-risk dormant cardholders get a different treatment (e.g. a call instead of messaging) rather than the same reminder sequence as everyone else? It would split the audience into different journeys and different channels/intensity, and would require a value or risk attribute that isn't currently exposed in this platform's Card/Account/Customer fields. Until then: Treat the whole dormant base as one uniform audience, consistent with the user's stated single-cause theory, and log the gap for a future platform enhancement if they do want tiering.
Defaults applied
  • Confirm the 10% holdout/control size is acceptable for this campaign. Affects how large a comparison group is withheld from messaging, trading reach for a cleaner read. Until then: Default to the tenant's stated preferred control of 10%.
Limitations
  • Transaction Events is marked new in the platform metadata: proposed, not confirmed as built in production. This campaign depends on it, so it cannot be presented as a verified platform capability.
  • Account.Status='Dormant' is the only buildable proxy for the user's '6 months no transaction' definition. Is the bank's internal Dormant threshold actually 6 months, or could it differ? If the internal threshold is shorter or longer than 6 months, the audience entering this campaign is not exactly the group the user described, which changes both reach and relevance.
  • Transaction Events (used for the goal) and Card Events are marked 'new — proposed, not confirmed built in production.' Can the team confirm these fire reliably before launch? If the goal event doesn't fire, the campaign can run but reactivation can't be measured, and the automatic goal-exit behaviour won't work either.

You
No target number yet. Success is more EMI Requests reaching Successful. On audience, our hunch is that higher balances convert better, roughly above 25,000 rupees, and that customers close to their due date feel more urgency. We think the main blocker is interest-cost hesitation, not awareness.
Agent
Entry triggers when an OS-to-EMI request is created and sitting Pending (the window before it auto-expires in 7 days). Because the user's belief is cost hesitation, not awareness, the first message leads with transparent interest/fee framing rather than an eligibility pitch — run as one arm of an A/B test against a tenure-clarity framing, since 'cost hesitation' and 'tenure/amount uncertainty' are different blockers with different fixes and the user has not ruled out the second. Reminders escalate urgency against the request's own 7-day expiry clock, lead with the cheapest channel and only step up to a costlier channel for reinforcement or delivery recovery. Two real targeting intentions — balance size and due-date proximity — cannot be built with what the platform exposes today, and are carried forward as limitations rather than approximated.
Approach
  • Entry on EMI_STATUS_CHANGED, New Status=Pending, Source=OS-to-EMI — the only available signal for 'a request now exists and hasn't resolved yet'; basis: tool (no eligibility-only event exists).
  • Goal on EMI_STATUS_CHANGED, New Status=Successful, Source=OS-to-EMI — directly proves the behaviour the user named; basis: user's stated success measure.
  • Message mechanism tested as an A/B experiment (cost-reassurance vs tenure-clarity first-touch) rather than assumed — basis: user named cost hesitation as a hunch, not a confirmed fact, and tenure/amount uncertainty is a plausible competing explanation worth separating per P-005.
  • Balance-based segmentation (>₹25,000) not built — basis: tool (no balance/utilization attribute exists anywhere in the entity list); this is a limitation, not a decision against the idea.
  • Due-date-proximity urgency not used as a targeting filter — basis: tool (cross-entity restriction); in-journey urgency instead keyed to the EMI request's own 7-day expiry, a different and weaker proxy for 'urgency' than due-date proximity, flagged as a trade-off.
  • Lead with EMAIL (lowest cost), escalate to SMS then WHATSAPP only for reinforcement or delivery recovery — basis: tenant preference 'prefer lower-cost channel first' and P-010.
Options weighed
  • Segmentation — cannot evaluate yet. The business case for prioritising higher balances is real and user-stated, but no attribute anywhere expresses outstanding balance or utilization, so there is nothing to segment on today. Needed: an Account or EMI Request attribute carrying a running outstanding-balance figure.
  • Experimentation — used. Cost-reassurance vs tenure-clarity first-touch message tests the user's 'interest-cost hesitation' hypothesis against a live competing explanation (tenure/amount uncertainty), changing one variable (message mechanism) per P-005.
  • Conditional branching — used. Branches on the reminder's delivery outcome (DELIVERED vs not) to decide whether to continue on the cheap channel or escalate — this is the only branch-worthy decision available (no account-attribute branching is reachable from a condition).
  • Channel fallback — used. No fallback-channel property exists on a send, so recovery is built as a condition on the prior send's delivery outcome: a failed SMS reminder routes to a WHATSAPP attempt; a delivered one continues on SMS.
  • Adaptive sequencing — used. Messages escalate urgency as the 7-day request-expiry clock runs down, since due-date proximity is unavailable as a targeting signal.
  • Cost and fatigue — used. Capped at 3 sends per customer path (within the 4-message limit), leading with EMAIL. The weakest message is the final reminder before expiry — kept because it is the last chance before the request auto-expires, which is high relevance despite being the costliest-channel option in the recovery arm.
  • Measurement and learning — used. A 10% control group (tenant preference) plus the message-mechanism A/B lets the business read which framing associates with more Successful outcomes. Without the holdout, any difference could reflect what would have happened anyway (P-006); with it, this is still an association, not a causal claim, until repeated over time.
Considered and not used
  • No drip campaign — handle entirely at the point of request (e.g. a single in-session nudge when the Pending request is created, no follow-up messages) — A single touch cannot re-engage someone who opens the request and then hesitates before the 7-day expiry; the brief's own hypothesis (interest-cost hesitation) implies people need reassurance more than once as the deadline approaches, so a short reminder sequence against a hard expiry window is the better fit. Trade-off: more messages, more fatigue risk, mitigated by the 4-message cap and 48h spacing.
Success criteria
  • More EMI Requests (Source=OS-to-EMI) reaching New Status=Successful — the business's own measure, no target figure set yet.
Measurement
  • Track count and rate of entrants whose EMI Request reaches Successful vs Expired/Failed/Cancelled, split by control vs treatment and by experiment arm (cost-reassurance vs tenure-clarity).
  • Track delivery outcome per channel/step to see how often the condition routes to the recovery (WHATSAPP) arm — this indicates channel reliability, not message effectiveness.
  • To measure properly: would need the balance/utilization figure for ex-post segmentation of results (even if not usable for live targeting yet), and a longer observation window across statement cycles to see if effects hold outside any one freeze/high-volume period.
Assumptions
  • DNC and NPA exclusion are enforced globally by the platform, not set per-campaign here.
  • Quiet hours (21:00–09:00) and the 48h minimum spacing are enforced by the platform automatically; no per-message time-of-day field exists in this blueprint to set directly.
  • EMI_STATUS_CHANGED is 'new-proposed' per platform metadata — designed against, but not confirmed live in production.
Hypotheses for future testing
  • Leading with interest/fee transparency reduces hesitation-driven drop-off more than a tenure-clarity framing does — untested, to be read from the A/B split.
  • Framing urgency around the request's own expiry countdown nudges completion before Expired — untested, no prior performance data exists for this bank.
Worth settling before this is built
  • Balance-based prioritisation (>₹25,000) cannot be built — no attribute exists anywhere for outstanding balance or utilization. Do you want to (a) proceed reaching all Pending OS-to-EMI requests regardless of balance, or (b) hold the campaign until such an attribute can be exposed to the builder? Changes who enters the campaign at all — proceeding without it means reaching a broader, unprioritised population than the user intended. Until then: Proceed with all Pending OS-to-EMI requests (no balance filter), and flag this as a standing limitation in every reporting cycle.
  • Due-date proximity cannot be used to target entry (cross-entity restriction). Is the in-journey substitute — urgency keyed to the EMI request's own 7-day expiry countdown — an acceptable stand-in for 'closer to their due date'? These are genuinely different clocks (statement due date vs request expiry); if the user specifically meant statement due date, the urgency messaging is solving a different moment than intended. Until then: Use the request's 7-day expiry countdown as the urgency signal, stated plainly as a substitution.
Defaults applied
  • Keep the tenant's preferred 10% control group for this campaign? Needed to read the A/B and overall campaign results as anything more than 'what happened', per P-006. Until then: Default to 10% control, matching stated tenant preference.
Limitations
  • EMI Events is marked new in the platform metadata: proposed, not confirmed as built in production. This campaign depends on it, so it cannot be presented as a verified platform capability.
  • EMI_STATUS_CHANGED (EMI Events) is marked 'new-proposed' in platform metadata, not confirmed built in production. Can this be confirmed live before launch? If this event isn't actually firing, neither entry nor goal can be measured at all.

Agent
The objective (lift OS-to-EMI — Outstanding-balance-to-EMI — conversions) maps onto real vocabulary here: EMI Request has a Product Type 'Outstanding' and a Source 'OS-to-EMI', and EMI_STATUS_CHANGED (New Status: Successful) looks like the natural goal event, subject to it being 'new-proposed' rather than confirmed live. Before I design the sequence I need to know how this business wants success judged (required before any proposal), and I need two things that change who enters and what the messages say: whether the opportunity is 'never started a conversion' versus 'started but stalled', and what's actually believed to be blocking conversion today. Both are things only the bank can tell me — the platform has no outstanding-balance field to target by size, so if that matters I need to flag it as a limitation rather than fake it with a proxy.

You
No target number yet. Success is more EMI Requests reaching Successful. On audience, our hunch is that higher balances convert better, roughly above 25,000 rupees, and that customers close to their due date feel more urgency. We think the main blocker is interest-cost hesitation, not awareness.
Agent
Enter customers as their statement due date approaches and send a short sequence that leads with interest-cost transparency, not product awareness, since the user believes hesitation over cost — not ignorance of the option — is what's blocking OS-to-EMI conversion. Goal is an EMI Request (Source = OS-to-EMI) reaching Successful; anyone who hits it exits automatically. No balance-based targeting is possible with current attributes, so reach is broader than the user's >25,000 hunch until that gap is resolved.
Approach
  • Entry on Account audience with Statement Due Date approaching, as a direct build of the user's 'urgency near due date' hypothesis — the only due-date-linked attribute the platform exposes.
  • Goal set to EMI_STATUS_CHANGED / New Status = Successful / Source = OS-to-EMI, so success is counted on the exact product line the user cares about, not any EMI conversion.
  • Lead with EMAIL (lowest cost) explaining fixed EMI and visible interest cost; reinforce with SMS then WhatsApp (higher cost, reserved for reinforcement per stated channel preference), each spaced the required 48h apart.
  • Branch once on the first send's delivery outcome: if EMAIL didn't deliver, recover on SMS immediately rather than waiting through a channel that already failed.
  • Include the preferred 10% control group as a standing practice, even though no lift is being claimed this round, so a future lift read is possible without redesigning the campaign.
Considered and not used
  • Entering on EMI_STATUS_CHANGED (Pending) to target customers who already started a request — Would target a different, already-engaged cohort and assumes 'stalled mid-request' is the dominant pattern; the user's stated barrier (hesitation before acting on cost) points more toward pre-request customers. Flagged as an open question rather than silently chosen.
  • Targeting by balance using Transaction Amount as a stand-in for outstanding balance — A single transaction's amount is not a customer's running outstanding balance — using it would quietly change who gets targeted. Left unbuilt and raised as a limitation instead.
  • An experiment (A/B) comparing two message framings this round — No prior performance data exists to size or motivate a specific variable test yet, and the user hasn't asked for one; kept to a single hypothesis per P-005 and reserved experimentation for a later round once this baseline runs.
Success criteria
  • User's own measure: more EMI Requests reaching Successful status. No fixed number or rate target was given.
Measurement
  • Track count and rate of EMI_STATUS_CHANGED → Successful events with Source = OS-to-EMI among journey entrants, compared against the 10% control group that receives no messages.
  • Track where in the funnel non-converters sit (Pending, Expired, Failed, Cancelled, or no request at all) — this shows where drop-off happens but does not by itself explain why.
  • To properly test the balance-size and due-date-urgency hunches, the platform would need an outstanding-balance or statement-balance attribute and the ability to combine Account and EMI Request conditions at entry — neither exists today.
Assumptions
  • Primary cohort is customers who have not yet started an OS-to-EMI request (opportunity-window stage), not those with a stalled Pending request — flagged for confirmation.
  • Statement Due Date can be scheduled as a rolling 'due date in the next ~10 days' window by the campaign manager at build time; exact day-count is a scheduling detail, defaulted here.
  • Audience is not filtered by balance size, since no attribute carries it — open to all eligible cardholders nearing their due date.
Hypotheses for future testing
  • Leading with a clear, upfront breakdown of interest cost — rather than a general product reminder — will reduce cost-hesitation-driven drop-off among customers who haven't yet converted their outstanding balance to EMI. This is untested; no performance history exists for this bank.
Defaults applied
  • How many days before the statement due date should the window open (e.g., 7 vs 10 vs 14 days)? Affects how many messages fit before the due date and whether urgency framing lands early enough to act on. Until then: Defaulting to a 10-day rolling window before due date, giving room for three 48h-spaced messages.
Limitations
  • EMI Events is marked new in the platform metadata: proposed, not confirmed as built in production. This campaign depends on it, so it cannot be presented as a verified platform capability.
  • There is no attribute anywhere (Account, Customer, Card, Transaction) representing outstanding or statement balance, so the user's >25,000 rupee hunch cannot be built as a targeting condition. The campaign will reach a broader group than the user intended; if balance truly predicts conversion, the audience the user asked for and the audience this reaches will differ in composition.
  • EMI_STATUS_CHANGED (used for both the goal and any Pending-stage targeting) is marked new-proposed, not confirmed built in production. If this event isn't actually firing in production yet, the goal check will never trigger and the campaign cannot report success at all.

You
No target number yet. Success is more EMI Requests reaching Successful. On audience, our hunch is that higher balances convert better, roughly above 25,000 rupees, and that customers close to their due date feel more urgency. We think the main blocker is interest-cost hesitation, not awareness.
Agent
Target customers who have an EMI-eligible outstanding transaction above ₹25,000 but have not yet converted it, and nudge them toward starting and completing an OS-to-EMI request. Lead with cost transparency rather than product awareness, since the stated blocker is interest-cost hesitation, and frame later touches around due-date urgency. Hold out 10% as a control so any difference in Successful conversions can be read against a real comparison group, per the bank's own preference.
Approach
  • Enter on a Transaction event (EMI Eligible = true, Amount > 25,000) rather than an audience snapshot, so the opportunity is caught close to when it appears, and so goal-check auto-exit removes anyone who converts mid-journey.
  • Lead with EMAIL (lowest cost) for the first touch, escalate to SMS then WHATSAPP for the two reminders, per the tenant's stated preference to lead low-cost and reserve higher-cost channels for reinforcement.
  • Every message leads with the cost/interest framing (fixed rate, no hidden fees) rather than 'did you know you can convert' framing, matching the stated blocker.
  • Keep the sequence to 3 sends across ~4-5 days (48h minimum spacing), inside the 4-message cap, since an EMI request stays open only 7 days before Expiry (P-003) and we don't want to message past that window.
  • Add a 10% control group so the business's own success measure (more Requests reaching Successful) can be read as a difference against a holdout, not just an absolute count.
Considered and not used
  • Entering on an Account audience segment filtered by Statement Due Date proximity instead of the Transaction event. — Would satisfy the due-date hunch directly, but would drop the balance-threshold hunch entirely since audience entry can only filter one entity's attributes, and Account has no balance field either. Chose balance-proxy entry and addressed urgency through copy instead.
  • Branching on whether a customer already has a Pending OS-to-EMI request (finish-what-you-started nudge). — Plausible and may be a bigger opportunity, but the user's answer didn't confirm this population should be in scope for this campaign; raised as an open question rather than silently added or dropped.
  • A fourth message / outcome-stage send. — Cap is 4 messages and minimum spacing is 48h; a 4th send would either breach spacing inside the 7-day request-expiry window or add a message with no new information. Three well-timed touches fit the window better.
Success criteria
  • Business's own measure: more EMI Requests (Source = OS-to-EMI) reaching New Status = Successful. No target number given yet.
Measurement
  • Track EMI_STATUS_CHANGED → Successful events among journey entrants (Source = OS-to-EMI, Product Type = Outstanding), split by treatment vs the 10% holdout, since no historical baseline exists to compare against otherwise.
  • Track delivery/open/click per send and, where visible, whether a Pending request appears after messaging, to see where in the funnel people stop — a drop-off at any one point does not by itself prove which message caused it.
  • To measure this properly we would need: confirmation that Transaction and EMI_STATUS_CHANGED events are live in production, and ideally a true outstanding-balance field so the ₹25,000 cut is applied to the right number rather than a single transaction's amount.
Assumptions
  • Transaction Events and EMI Events (EMI_STATUS_CHANGED) are both marked 'new-proposed' in platform metadata — not confirmed live. The goal and entry both depend on them.
  • DNC and NPA exclusions are enforced by the platform as stated tenant-wide constraints; no customer attribute for either is exposed here to filter on directly.
  • Statement Due Date exists on Account but there's no confirmed way to express a rolling 'due date within N days of today' entry filter from this tool set, so due-date urgency is handled via message timing/copy, not a hard audience cut.
Hypotheses for future testing
  • Leading with upfront, fixed-cost framing will reduce interest-cost hesitation enough to move more eligible customers from no action to a Successful EMI request (untested).
  • Reminders timed in the days around statement due date increase completion urgency more than evenly-spaced generic reminders (untested, and only approximated here since we can't target each customer's actual due date).
Defaults applied
  • Confirm the 10% control group is acceptable for this campaign. Needed to read 'more Requests reaching Successful' as an effect rather than just an absolute count. Until then: Default to the tenant's stated preferred control percentage of 10%.
Limitations
  • Transaction Events is marked new in the platform metadata: proposed, not confirmed as built in production. This campaign depends on it, so it cannot be presented as a verified platform capability.
  • EMI Events is marked new in the platform metadata: proposed, not confirmed as built in production. This campaign depends on it, so it cannot be presented as a verified platform capability.
  • Transaction Events and EMI Events (EMI_STATUS_CHANGED) are marked new/proposed, not confirmed built in production. Can these be confirmed live before launch? Both the entry trigger and the goal depend on these categories; if they're not live, neither will fire.
  • No attribute for total outstanding balance exists on Customer or Account. Is a single EMI-eligible transaction's amount (>₹25,000) an acceptable stand-in for 'balance above ₹25,000', or should this wait until a true balance field is exposed? The audience actually reached may differ from the one you intended — some customers with a qualifying total balance but no single transaction above ₹25,000 will be missed, and some with one large eligible transaction but a lower true outstanding balance will be included.
Still unknown
  • Whether Transaction and EMI Request events are actually emitting from production systems today.
  • Whether a true outstanding-balance attribute could be exposed in future to replace the transaction-amount proxy.
Generate this campaign?

Nothing has been built yet. Confirm to create the journey, or tell the agent what to change.

OS-to-EMI Conversion Nudge — Cost Transparency · control 10%

Targets customers with an EMI-eligible outstanding transaction above ₹25,000 who have not converted it to EMI. Leads with upfront cost/interest transparency to address interest-cost hesitation, with two spaced reminders building due-date urgency, inside a 10% holdout for measurement.

You
No target number yet. Success is more EMI Requests reaching Successful. On audience, our hunch is that higher balances convert better, roughly above 25,000 rupees, and that customers close to their due date feel more urgency. We think the main blocker is interest-cost hesitation, not awareness.
Agent
Target cardholders with an active account approaching their statement due date, and nudge them toward an OS-to-EMI request with messaging that leads with cost clarity rather than product awareness, since the stated blocker is interest-cost hesitation. Three spaced messages across the pre-due-date window, each respecting the 48-hour minimum gap, with the platform's automatic goal check removing anyone who converts mid-journey.
Approach
  • Entry on an Account audience segment (Status = Active, Statement Due Date within an approaching window) rather than an event, because the opportunity is a standing account state, not a one-off event — this matches the user's timing hunch directly.
  • Goal on EMI_STATUS_CHANGED where New Status = Successful and Source = OS-to-EMI — the only event that proves the behaviour happened, read from the EMI Request entity.
  • Messages lead with lower-cost channel (EMAIL) then step up to SMS and WHATSAPP for reinforcement, per the tenant's stated preference to lead with the cheaper channel.
  • Copy reassures on interest/cost and simplifies the ask (fixed monthly amount, few taps) rather than explaining what EMI is, because the user's working theory is cost hesitation, not unawareness.
  • A waitForEvent on EMI_STATUS_CHANGED with a 7-day timeout follows the last send, matching the platform's own 7-day request-expiry window (P-003), so the journey doesn't run past the point a request would auto-expire.
Considered and not used
  • Filter entry by Outstanding Balance > ₹25,000 — No attribute exists for outstanding balance on Account or Customer. Substituting Transaction Amount would misrepresent a per-transaction figure as a balance and was rejected rather than faked.
  • Branch the journey by balance tier (high vs low) to message them differently — No buildable balance attribute to branch on; a tiered message strategy would require data the platform cannot filter on today.
  • Use EMI Events entry (e.g. enter on EMI Request created) instead of account state — That would enter customers who already started a request — too late for an intervention meant to prompt the request itself.
  • 4 sends to fill the message cap — 3 sends spaced 48h apart plus a 7-day wait-for-event already covers the window to due date and the request-expiry period; a 4th send would add fatigue risk without a clear new job.
Success criteria
  • Business's own measure (as given): more EMI Requests reaching New Status = Successful. No target rate was set.
Measurement
  • Track EMI Requests with Source = OS-to-EMI by New Status (Pending/Successful/Failed/Expired/Cancelled) for entrants vs the control group, since a control group is the only way to separate this from what would have happened anyway (P-006).
  • Track message delivery outcomes per channel (DELIVERED, FAILED_* etc.) to separate a message that didn't land from a message that landed but didn't convert.
  • To properly measure interest-cost hesitation as the blocker, aggregated pre/post click-through on cost-related content, or a qualitative customer survey, would help — neither exists in this prototype, so treat the blocker as a hypothesis the copy is built around, not a confirmed cause.
Assumptions
  • Account Status = Active is used as the closest available proxy for excluding NPA/charged-off accounts, since no explicit NPA attribute exists; 'Charge off' and similar statuses are excluded by this filter.
  • DNC suppression is enforced by the platform at send time as a hard constraint, not as an audience condition, since no DNC attribute appears in the attribute catalogue.
  • The approaching-due-date window is treated as a relative date range (e.g., due date falls within the next several days); exact day-count is an implementation default, not a business decision.
Hypotheses for future testing
  • Leading with interest-cost clarity (fixed monthly amount, no surprise charges) will reduce cost-hesitation friction more than a purely informational message — untested.
  • Messaging timed to due-date proximity will read as more urgent and relevant than a flat-rate send — untested.
Worth settling before this is built
  • The >₹25,000 balance hunch can't be enforced as an audience filter today — there is no Outstanding Balance attribute on Account or Customer. Do you want this campaign to run on ALL active accounts approaching due date (broader reach, balance-agnostic), or is there an issuer-configured Smart Tag that already marks high-balance customers that I should ask the platform team to confirm? Determines whether the campaign is intentionally broad (accepting lower average relevance per the conservative 'fewer, better-targeted messages' preference) or waits on a tag being confirmed before launch. Until then: Run on all active accounts approaching due date, without a balance filter, and flag the balance hunch as unimplemented targeting.
Defaults applied
  • How many days before the statement due date should entry trigger (e.g., 3, 5, 7 days out)? Too early loses urgency; too late leaves no room for the 48h-spaced 3-message sequence before due date. Until then: Default to a window opening 7 days before due date, giving room for 3 sends at 48h spacing plus a short buffer.
Limitations
  • EMI Events is marked new in the platform metadata: proposed, not confirmed as built in production. This campaign depends on it, so it cannot be presented as a verified platform capability.
  • EMI_STATUS_CHANGED (the event this goal and the closing wait depend on) is marked 'new/proposed' in the event catalogue, not confirmed live in production. If this event isn't actually emitted yet, the goal can't be measured and the closing wait-for-event step won't resolve — the journey would only end by timeout.
Still unknown
  • Whether an issuer-configured Smart Tag already encodes a high-balance or EMI-propensity segment — Smart Tag values exist as a type but no real values are visible from here to verify or select.
  • Whether EMI_STATUS_CHANGED and its New Status/Source conditions are live in production or still the proposed version flagged in the event catalogue.

OS-to-EMI Conversion Nudge · control 10%

Prompts active cardholders approaching their statement due date to convert outstanding balance to EMI, leading with interest-cost reassurance since that is the believed blocker. Three spaced messages, lowest-cost channel first, with an automatic goal exit on conversion and a closing wait matched to the platform's 7-day request-expiry window.

entry: {"kind": "audience", "entity": "Account", "conditions": [{"attribute": "Status", "operator": "Equals", "value": "Active"}, {"attribute": "Statement Due Date", "operator": "Less than", "value": "+7 days"}]}
goal : {"eventCategory": "EMI Events", "eventType": "EMI_STATUS_CHANGED", "conditions": [{"attribute": "New Status", "operator": "Equals", "value": "Successful"}, {"attribute": "Source", "operator": "Equals", "value": "OS-to-EMI"}]}
  1. SEND Intro: EMI option with cost clarity EMAIL
    Hi ${customerFirstName}, you can split your outstanding card balance into fixed monthly instalments. No surprise charges, just one clear amount each month. See your option before your due date.
    cta View my EMI option
  2. WAIT 48h
    Minimum spacing between messages; gives time to act on the first message before a reminder.
  3. SEND Reminder: due date approaching SMS
    Reminder: your due date is coming up. Convert your outstanding balance to EMI in a few taps and know your monthly amount upfront.
    cta Convert now
  4. WAIT 48h
    Second minimum-spacing gap before the final nudge.
  5. SEND Final nudge before due date WHATSAPP
    ${customerFirstName}, there's still time. Turn your outstanding balance into easy EMIs and see your fixed monthly amount before your due date.
    cta See my EMI amount
  6. WAIT FOR EVENT EMI Events/EMI_STATUS_CHANGED · timeout 7d
  7. EXIT
    No EMI request reached Successful within the request's active window; journey ends.

You
Success is a rise in completed OS-to-EMI conversions among customers who enter, measured against the control group. Target customers who already have a pending request. Keep targeting broad at Source = OS-to-EMI, no Product Type narrowing.
Agent
Enter customers the moment their OS-to-EMI request is created (New Status = Pending), and nudge them across the 7-day window EMI requests stay open before expiring (P-003). Goal is the request moving to Successful. A 10% control group is held out so any observed difference in completion rate can be attributed to the campaign rather than natural completion. Messaging leads with the cheapest channel and escalates only if the customer hasn't converted, respecting the 48-hour minimum spacing and 4-message cap.
Approach
  • Entry on EMI_STATUS_CHANGED (EMI Request entity) with Source = OS-to-EMI AND New Status = Pending — this is the only event that captures 'a pending request now exists', per the sequence analysis; flagged as new-proposed, not a verified production event.
  • Goal on EMI_STATUS_CHANGED with Source = OS-to-EMI AND New Status = Successful — the proof-point the business asked for (completed conversions). The platform auto-exits anyone who hits this at any point, so later steps only reach people who haven't yet converted.
  • Three reminder touches at 48h+ spacing (EMAIL → SMS → WHATSAPP, cheapest-first), sized to fit inside the 7-day expiry window without exceeding the 4-message cap.
  • A waitForEvent step absorbs the remainder of the 7-day window so the journey doesn't force a 4th send before the deadline has actually passed.
  • A final outcome message only reaches customers who are still in-journey (i.e., did not convert) after the window closes — it does not promise a new offer, it informs and gives a next step.
  • 10% control group held out (stated preference) so the lift can be measured; no other segmentation layer added since Product Type and amount-based narrowing were both ruled out.
Considered and not used
  • Narrow by Product Type (Outstanding only) — User explicitly asked for broad targeting at Source = OS-to-EMI with no Product Type narrowing.
  • Target pre-request / top-of-funnel customers via a generic offer-issuance event — User chose the pending-request stage; also Outcome Issuance has no entity-based conditions, so it cannot be confirmed to map to OS-to-EMI offers specifically.
  • Filter by outstanding balance size — No such field exists on any entity (Account, Customer, EMI Request, Transaction). Cannot be built regardless of preference.
  • Branch the journey by delivery outcome (e.g. SMS failed → fallback channel) — The builder only supports a condition on the previous send's delivery outcome, not a routed fallback channel on one send. Adding this would need an extra condition step per send for marginal benefit; kept the journey linear for simplicity given the short 7-day window.
  • 4th reminder squeezed in before the deadline — Minimum 48h spacing and the 7-day expiry ceiling don't comfortably fit a 4th reminder plus an outcome message; prioritised one outcome message over an extra reminder.
Success criteria
  • Business's own measure (as given): a rise in completed OS-to-EMI conversions among campaign entrants, compared to the control group that received no messages.
Measurement
  • Track entry volume, per-step delivery status (DELIVERED/OPENED/CLICKED etc. per list_channels), goal-reached count and timing for treatment vs. the 10% control group.
  • Compare the Successful-conversion rate (goal hit) of treatment vs. control over the 7-day window, not in isolation — a change in the treatment group alone proves nothing without the control comparison (P-006).
  • To measure properly over time you'd want this run repeatedly across cohorts with the major variable (e.g. channel order, message count) held constant per run (P-005), since no historical performance data exists yet to compare against (P-001/P-002 give rough industry-wide base rates only, not this campaign's expected result).
Assumptions
  • EMI_STATUS_CHANGED fires promptly when an EMI Request is created as Pending and again when it resolves — unverified since the event category is marked new-proposed.
  • Quiet hours, DNC and NPA exclusion are enforced automatically by the platform as stated guardrails; no per-customer override is available (P-004).
Hypotheses for future testing
  • Reminding customers of a pending request they already started removes a simple 'forgot to finish' friction and may lift completion before the 7-day expiry — untested, no prior data exists for this bank.
Defaults applied
  • Keep the 10% control group default, or use a different holdout percentage? Affects how many customers are excluded from messaging and the statistical basis for the lift comparison. Until then: Default to 10%, per the stated tenant preference.
  • Is the exact reminder cadence (immediate, +48h, +96h, then wait out the window) acceptable, or do you want fewer/more touches inside the 7 days? Changes message fatigue risk and how much of the 7-day window is used for nudging vs. waiting. Until then: Default to the 3-reminder + 1-outcome sequence described, which respects the 4-message cap and 48h minimum spacing.
Limitations
  • EMI Events is marked new in the platform metadata: proposed, not confirmed as built in production. This campaign depends on it, so it cannot be presented as a verified platform capability.
  • EMI_STATUS_CHANGED (and the EMI Request entity it filters) is marked new/proposed, not confirmed built in production. Can you confirm it's live before this launches? If it isn't live, neither the entry trigger nor the goal can fire, and the campaign needs a different, verified trigger (e.g. a confirmed-production event the campaign manager supplies).
Still unknown
  • Whether EMI_STATUS_CHANGED is actually live in production for this tenant — if not, neither entry nor goal can fire and the whole campaign needs a different trigger the campaign manager would need to supply.

On screenawaiting-confirmation83.2s
You
Read success as the Pending to Successful conversion rate versus the control group. Absolute volume is secondary. That all looks right, go ahead.
Agent
Customers land in the journey the moment their OS-to-EMI request is created and still Pending — the only point where nudging can still change the outcome. The journey sends up to three escalating reminders inside the 7-day window the request stays open before auto-expiring, then stops. The platform auto-exits anyone who reaches Successful after any step, so live conversions are never double-messaged. A 10% holdout lets the user read true incremental lift on Pending→Successful, which is the success measure they confirmed.
Approach
  • Entry on EMI_STATUS_CHANGED (New Status=Pending, Source=OS-to-EMI) rather than an earlier 'offer appeared' event, because that's the first point a real, unconverted request exists and the customer can still act on it.
  • Goal on EMI_STATUS_CHANGED (New Status=Successful, Source=OS-to-EMI) — a different event on the same entity, which proves the behaviour rather than just naming it.
  • Three sends spaced 48h apart (the enforced minimum), fitting inside the 7-day expiry window (P-003) with buffer before expiry, respecting the 4-message cap.
  • Lead with EMAIL (cheapest, P-010), escalate to SMS then WhatsApp for later reminders — cost-conscious but reinforcing urgency as expiry nears.
  • 10% control group held out with no messaging, so Pending→Successful can be compared against a true counterfactual (P-006).
Considered and not used
  • Enter customers earlier, at whatever event signals eligibility for OS-to-EMI (e.g. a qualifying transaction) — That event marks opportunity, not an existing unconverted request — it would include customers who never actually started a request, diluting the audience and the read on this specific conversion step.
  • Branch mid-journey on EMI Request status (e.g. detect Failed vs still-Pending) — Conditions can only test the previous send's delivery outcome, not entry-event or entity attributes mid-journey. This is a real builder gap, not a design choice — flagged as a limitation below.
  • Segment messaging by outstanding balance size — No attribute links EMI Request to a balance/amount; would require inventing a non-existent join.
  • A fourth reminder right before the 7-day expiry — Would push total messages to 4 back-to-back within a day of the 48h-spaced third message, cutting too close to minimum spacing and risking fatigue on a single-digit-conversion funnel (P-001) for marginal reach.
Success criteria
  • Primary: Pending→Successful conversion rate for the treatment group vs the 10% control holdout, read directly as requested.
  • Absolute count/value of completed OS-to-EMI conversions tracked as secondary context, not the deciding metric.
Measurement
  • Track: entries (Pending created, OS-to-EMI), sends/deliveries per step, Goal reached count and timing relative to entry, and terminal EMI status (Successful/Failed/Expired/Cancelled) for both treatment and control.
  • Evaluate: compare treatment vs control Pending→Successful rate over the same entry cohort window; do not compare treatment-only before/after, since that can't separate campaign effect from normal behaviour (P-006).
  • To measure properly: would need the campaign manager to confirm EMI_STATUS_CHANGED is actually live in production (it's currently marked new-proposed) and to pull cohort-level conversion counts after a run — no historical performance data exists yet to benchmark against.
Assumptions
  • DNC and NPA exclusions and quiet-hour suppression are enforced by the platform automatically and don't need to be re-expressed as blueprint conditions — I found no attribute value for 'NPA' to encode this explicitly even if I wanted to.
  • A Pending OS-to-EMI request is the right and only entry point; requests that go straight to Failed without a Pending state (if any) are out of scope since no event captures them as an open opportunity.
  • EMI_STATUS_CHANGED will be available by the time this runs — if not, this entire design has no valid entry/goal event and needs an alternative signal.
Hypotheses for future testing
  • Reminding customers of a still-open, time-limited request reduces passive drop-off caused by forgetting — untested.
  • Escalating channel cost/urgency (email → SMS → WhatsApp) as expiry nears may recover more conversions than a flat single-channel sequence — untested.
Data that would improve this
  • What does the real distribution of time-to-convert or time-to-expire look like within the 7-day OS-to-EMI window? Would let wait durations be tuned to when customers actually act, rather than to the regulatory minimum spacing alone.
Defaults applied
  • Confirm the channel escalation order (EMAIL first-touch → SMS reminder → WhatsApp final reminder) is acceptable, versus leading with SMS for higher urgency given it's a time-limited, auth-triggered request. Changes cost profile and open-rate assumptions; EMAIL-first is the cost-conservative default per tenant preference. Until then: Default to EMAIL → SMS → WhatsApp as proposed.
Limitations
  • EMI Events is marked new in the platform metadata: proposed, not confirmed as built in production. This campaign depends on it, so it cannot be presented as a verified platform capability.
  • EMI_STATUS_CHANGED and the EMI Request entity are marked 'new-proposed' — not confirmed built in production. Can the campaign manager confirm this event actually fires in production before this goes live? If it isn't live, neither the entry trigger nor the goal event exists, and this entire blueprint has no valid signal to run on.
Still unknown
  • Whether EMI_STATUS_CHANGED and the EMI Request entity are confirmed live in production (metadata marks them new-proposed).
  • Typical real-world time-to-convert or time-to-expire distribution within the 7-day window, which would help tune wait durations beyond the regulatory minimum spacing.

Blueprint behind the confirm button

OS-to-EMI Pending Conversion Nudge · control 10%

Reminds customers with a Pending OS-to-EMI request to complete it before the 7-day expiry, using an escalating low-to-higher-cost channel sequence, with a 10% holdout for lift measurement.

entry: {"kind": "event", "eventCategory": "EMI Events", "eventType": "EMI_STATUS_CHANGED", "conditions": [{"attribute": "New Status", "operator": "Equals", "value": "Pending"}, {"attribute": "Source", "operator": "Equals", "value": "OS-to-EMI"}]}
goal : {"eventCategory": "EMI Events", "eventType": "EMI_STATUS_CHANGED", "conditions": [{"attribute": "New Status", "operator": "Equals", "value": "Successful"}, {"attribute": "Source", "operator": "Equals", "value": "OS-to-EMI"}]}
  1. SEND Pending request first nudge EMAIL
    Hi ${customerFirstName}, you started converting your outstanding balance into easy EMIs but it's not done yet. Finish it in a couple of taps.
    cta Complete your EMI request
  2. WAIT 48h
    Minimum enforced spacing between messages; also gives the customer time to act before following up.
  3. SEND Pending request reminder SMS
    ${customerFirstName}, your request to convert your outstanding balance to EMI is still open. Complete it now to start paying in smaller installments.
    cta Finish now
  4. WAIT 48h
    Maintains minimum spacing; keeps total journey length (4 days so far) safely inside the 7-day expiry window.
  5. SEND Final pending request reminder WHATSAPP
    ${customerFirstName}, your outstanding-to-EMI request closes soon. Complete it today to keep this option before it expires.
    cta Convert before it expires
  6. EXIT
    No conversion recorded within the campaign sequence; request will auto-expire per its own 7-day rule if left untouched.

You
No, keep this campaign focused on customers who already have a Pending request. We will look at the earlier stage separately once the event exists.
Agent
Target customers who already have a Pending OS-to-EMI request and have not yet converted. The hypothesis is that some of these customers simply forget or drop off mid-flow, so a short, spaced reminder sequence with an easy entry point back into the flow can recover some of them before the request expires in 7 days. Sequence starts on the cheapest channel and escalates to WhatsApp for the final, most urgent nudge, within the 4-message cap and 48-hour spacing rule.
Approach
  • Entry on EMI_STATUS_CHANGED = Pending, Source = OS-to-EMI — this is the point where the behaviour (converting to EMI) has not yet happened but the customer has already acted (request exists), which is the right place to intervene.
  • Goal on EMI_STATUS_CHANGED = Successful, Source = OS-to-EMI — this is the only event that proves the behaviour (conversion) happened; it sits on a different event/status than entry, which is correct and expected.
  • Four sends spaced 48h apart (day 0, 2, 4, 6), fitting inside the 7-day expiry window with a final wait to day 7 before the path closes — uses the full message cap without exceeding the window.
  • Channel order EMAIL → SMS → WHATSAPP → WHATSAPP: cheapest first, WhatsApp repeated for the final two touches since those carry the most urgency and reinforcement value.
  • 10% control group held out per tenant preference, so any future read of this campaign's effect can be separated from what would have happened anyway (P-006) — though no lift is claimed here, only a hypothesis.
Considered and not used
  • Entry earlier, e.g. off statement generation or an eligible-outstanding-balance signal — User explicitly scoped this campaign to the Pending-request stage only; that earlier stage has no qualifying event available yet and was deferred to a separate campaign.
  • Branch mid-journey into a distinct message for customers whose request fails or expires — The condition step can only read the previous send's delivery outcome, not EMI Request status, so this branch cannot be built here. Raised as an operational limitation rather than faked.
  • Use Transaction Events as entry/goal — Transaction events describe payment activity, not EMI request state, and the category is also marked new/proposed. EMI_STATUS_CHANGED is the correct entity for this objective even though it carries the same new-proposed caveat.
  • 5th message using the remaining day-7 slack — Message cap is 4; adding a 5th would violate it. Used the slack as a final wait instead so the goal-check still fires right up to expiry.
Assumptions
  • DNC suppression and NPA exclusion are applied automatically by the platform as stated in constraints; no manual condition is added for them.
  • Quiet hours (21:00–09:00) and the festive freeze (Nov 7–21, 2026) are enforced by the scheduler, not by this blueprint; flagged in case this campaign is live during that freeze window.
  • The EMI_STATUS_CHANGED event category is marked new/proposed, not confirmed built in production — this entire entry and goal depend on it actually existing.
Worth settling before this is built
  • Should Product Type also be constrained to 'Outstanding' alongside Source = 'OS-to-EMI', in case Source alone is broader than intended? If Source='OS-to-EMI' already uniquely identifies this product flow, the extra filter is redundant; if not, omitting it could pull in adjacent EMI products. Until then: Assuming Source = 'OS-to-EMI' alone is sufficient to scope the cohort, since it names the flow directly; Product Type filter not added.

On screenawaiting-confirmation82.5s
You
Yes, include them. Honestly that is the bigger opportunity — most customers never start an OS-to-EMI request at all, they just carry the balance and pay interest.
Agent
This adds a second, parallel journey to the OS-to-EMI programme: a conversion-creation campaign for customers who are carrying an EMI-eligible balance but have never started a request, sitting alongside the pending-request nudge already proposed. Since the builder has no 'customer carries an outstanding balance, no request yet' event, entry uses the closest real proxy: a settled transaction flagged EMI Eligible. The goal is deliberately set at request-Pending (not Successful), so each campaign owns one measurable behaviour change and the two journeys hand off cleanly instead of overlapping on the same goal.
Approach
  • Entry on Transaction / Transaction Status=SETTLED / EMI Eligible=true: the best available signal that an eligible balance now exists for this customer, used as a proxy for 'opportunity appears' since no Account-level 'carries eligible outstanding balance' flag is exposed.
  • Goal on EMI_STATUS_CHANGED / New Status=Pending / Source=OS-to-EMI — proves the specific behaviour this campaign can influence (starting a request), not the eventual payoff. Successful conversion is the pending-nudge campaign's job, avoiding two campaigns claiming credit for the same outcome.
  • 3 sends, cheapest channel first (EMAIL→SMS→WHATSAPP), 48h apart: benefit framing, then friction-reduction, then a final reinforcement — no fixed external deadline exists here (unlike the 7-day Pending expiry), so pacing is set by fatigue avoidance (P-011) and the message cap rather than a countdown.
  • 10% control group held out per stated preference, so if this is measured later the effect can be separated from baseline conversion-to-EMI behaviour (P-006) — no lift is claimed now.
  • Once a customer starts a request (reaches Pending) they exit this journey automatically via the goal check and become eligible for the separately proposed pending-nudge campaign — the two are designed to hand off, not run double messages on the same person.
Considered and not used
  • Entry on Account Smart Tag flagged as 'EMI-eligible balance' — Smart Tag values are issuer-configured and no allowed-value list exists in this prototype, so a condition here cannot be verified and risks matching nobody or everybody.
  • Use the pending-request campaign's EMI_STATUS_CHANGED entry for this cohort too — That event only fires once a request already exists — it cannot see customers who never started one, which is exactly the population this round adds.
  • Set this campaign's goal to Successful (full conversion) — A single message sequence that fires before any request exists has no visibility into what happens during underwriting/approval; crediting it with the final Successful status would conflate two different mechanisms (starting vs completing).
  • Restrict Transaction Type to a specific list (e.g. exclude EMI_PRINCIPAL/EMI_INTEREST) — The Transaction Type field only supports 'Any of' (inclusion), not exclusion, so I cannot reliably filter out transactions that are already part of an existing EMI without risking excluding valid eligible transactions too; left unfiltered and flagged as an assumption instead.
Assumptions
  • EMI Eligible=true on a SETTLED transaction is treated as reasonable evidence of an unconverted, convertible balance, even though it is a transaction-level flag and not a direct account-balance state.
  • DNC and NPA exclusions are enforced as global send-time guardrails by the platform, since this entry type cannot itself carry an Account-level exclusion condition.
  • Quiet hours are applied automatically by the scheduler.
Worth settling before this is built
  • Should entry be restricted to specific Transaction Types (e.g. only purchase-type postings) to better approximate 'carries an outstanding balance', or is any EMI-eligible settled transaction an acceptable trigger? Transaction Type can only be included via 'Any of', not excluded, so this changes who enters and could pull in transactions unrelated to a revolving balance (e.g. already-converted EMI postings). Until then: Launch with EMI Eligible=true and Transaction Status=SETTLED only, no Transaction Type restriction.
Defaults applied
  • Is 10% the right control-group size for this cohort too, given it is likely a much larger audience than the already-pending cohort? A larger audience can usually afford a smaller holdout without hurting measurement power; 10% here may hold back more reach than needed. Until then: Default to the stated 10% preference.
Limitations
  • Transaction Events is marked new in the platform metadata: proposed, not confirmed as built in production. This campaign depends on it, so it cannot be presented as a verified platform capability.
  • EMI Events is marked new in the platform metadata: proposed, not confirmed as built in production. This campaign depends on it, so it cannot be presented as a verified platform capability.
  • Both Transaction Events and EMI Events are marked new/proposed, not confirmed built in production. This entire journey's entry and goal depend on both categories. If either isn't actually live, the journey cannot run as designed.
1Should entry be restricted to specific Transaction Types (e.g. only purchase-type postings) to better approximate 'carries an outstanding balance', or is any EMI-eligible settled transaction an acceptable trigger?

Before we build it: does the size of the outstanding balance matter here?
Agent
Target customers with an open, still-Pending OS-to-EMI request and nudge them to complete the conversion before the request expires at day 7. Entry and goal both sit on EMI Request so the behaviour, the proof of success, and the deadline are all evidenced by the same entity. Outstanding-balance size cannot be used as a filter here because no amount/balance attribute exists on EMI Request — that's a platform limitation, not a design choice, and is explained below rather than worked around.
Approach
  • Entry: EMI_STATUS_CHANGED, New Status=Pending, Source=OS-to-EMI — the one point this platform can evidence where the request exists but isn't yet resolved.
  • Goal: EMI_STATUS_CHANGED, New Status=Successful, Source=OS-to-EMI — the event that proves conversion; platform auto-exits anyone who reaches it (P-008), so messaging stops the moment they convert.
  • Three nudges at the minimum 48h spacing (EMAIL → SMS → WHATSAPP, cheapest-first per preference) spread across the 7-day open window, each with a different angle: benefit reminder, progress nudge, urgency.
  • A 4th message only if the request is still unresolved near day 7 — a close-of-window note — staying within the 4-message cap.
  • 10% control group held out per stated preference so a future lift analysis is possible (P-006); no lift is being claimed now.
Considered and not used
  • Filter or segment by outstanding-balance size at entry — EMI Request (the entity this journey's entry/goal filter on) exposes only New Status, Product Type and Source — no amount or balance attribute exists on it. The only entity with a numeric amount is Transaction, which belongs to a different event category entirely.
  • Switch entry to a Transaction event so Transaction Amount becomes filterable — Transaction events only confirm EMI-eligibility generically, not that an OS-to-EMI request specifically exists; this would blur in Txn-to-EMI and Multi-Txn-to-EMI activity and lose the precise, product-specific signal EMI Request gives us.
  • Also target customers with an eligible balance but no request started yet — Already raised and answered in round 1 — no event in this platform currently exposes 'customer has eligible balance, no request yet,' so that audience is out of scope for this campaign as designed.
Assumptions
  • DNC and NPA exclusion are enforced globally by the platform at send time, since this event-based entry cannot itself carry Account-level exclusion conditions.
  • Quiet hours (21:00–09:00) are applied automatically by the scheduler.
  • All pending OS-to-EMI requests, regardless of balance size, receive the same messaging sequence.
Defaults applied
  • Is 10% control group size right for this specific, already-narrow Pending-OS-to-EMI audience? A larger holdout gives cleaner future measurement; a smaller one reaches more customers now. Until then: Default to the stated 10% preference.
Limitations
  • EMI Events is marked new in the platform metadata: proposed, not confirmed as built in production. This campaign depends on it, so it cannot be presented as a verified platform capability.
  • EMI Request has no amount/balance attribute exposed for conditions, so balance size cannot segment this campaign today. If the bank wants different messaging or thresholds for large vs small outstanding balances, that requires a new attribute on EMI Request (or a different entry entity with the trade-offs noted above).
  • EMI_STATUS_CHANGED (EMI Events) is marked new/proposed, not confirmed built in production. Both entry and goal depend on this event; if it isn't live, the journey cannot run as designed.

  • Goal on EMI_STATUS_CHANGED / New Status=Successful / Source=OS-to-EMI: the event that actually proves conversion, on the same entity, so it fires independently of the messages and the platform auto-exits anyone who converts mid-journey (P-008).

  • Branch customers by delivery outcome of each send — Delivery-outcome conditions tell us whether a message arrived, not whether the customer converted; the goal check already handles the conversion-relevant branching automatically.
  • Add a 5th reminder inside the window — Message cap is 4 and 48h minimum spacing already fills the 7-day window; a 5th message would need <48h spacing or exceed the cap.

On screenawaiting-confirmation97.7s
You
Yes, include them. Honestly that is the bigger opportunity — most customers never start an OS-to-EMI request at all, they just carry the balance and pay interest.
Agent
This is a second, separate campaign from the pending-request nudge, because it targets a fundamentally different population with a different entry signal: customers who are currently being charged interest on a carried balance and have never started an OS-to-EMI request. The builder only supports one entry trigger per journey, so the two audiences cannot be OR'd into a single blueprint. Entry fires on a system-generated INTEREST transaction (the clearest available proxy for 'carrying a revolving balance'); the goal is the same OS-to-EMI Successful conversion event used in the pending-request campaign, so results from both are comparable later.
Approach
  • Entry on Transaction Events / Transaction Type=INTEREST, Status=SETTLED, Initiated By=SYSTEM_GENERATED — this is the only available event that evidences 'customer is carrying a balance and paying interest', which is exactly the behaviour the user described as the untapped opportunity.
  • Goal kept identical to the pending-request campaign (EMI_STATUS_CHANGED, New Status=Successful, Product Type=Outstanding, Source=OS-to-EMI) so both campaigns prove the same outcome and can eventually be compared.
  • Three sends only (first-touch EMAIL, reminder SMS, reinforcement WHATSAPP), cheapest channel first, 48h apart — this audience has no hard deadline (no expiry event exists for 'never started'), so there's no reason to fill the full 4-message cap; fewer, better-targeted messages fits the stated conservative risk appetite.
  • 10% control group held out, since no lift can be claimed without one.
  • No waitForEvent / deadline step used — unlike a pending EMI request (which expires in 7 days per P-003), there is no expiry event for a customer who simply never initiates. The campaign ends after the third touch; the platform's automatic goal-check still exits anyone who converts mid-sequence.
Considered and not used
  • Filter the Transaction-entry to also exclude customers with an existing Pending/Successful EMI Request — Entry conditions can only use attributes of the entity the category filters (Transaction), not EMI Request. This cross-entity exclusion is not expressible here — flagged as a limitation below.
  • Use Transaction EMI Eligible=true as the entry signal instead of Transaction Type=INTEREST — EMI Eligible appears to flag a specific purchase as convertible (fits Txn-to-EMI / Multi-Txn-to-EMI products), not a carried revolving balance. INTEREST being charged is closer evidence of the Outstanding/OS-to-EMI situation the user described.
  • Combine this with the pending-request campaign into one journey — One journey = one entry trigger in this builder; the two populations enter at genuinely different moments (opportunity-exists vs request-already-started) and merging would blur which message a given customer should see first.
  • Fill all 4 message slots with reminders — No deadline forces urgency for this audience, and the stated preference is fewer, better-targeted messages over broad reach.
Assumptions
  • An INTEREST transaction with status SETTLED, system-generated, is a reasonable proxy for 'customer is currently carrying a revolving balance' — it is not a perfect eligibility flag, since this blueprint cannot also check that no OS-to-EMI request already exists for that customer.
  • No minimum interest/balance amount threshold is applied (catches any interest charge, however small); a threshold could sharpen targeting but none was specified.
  • DNC and NPA exclusions, quiet hours, and the festive freeze (7–21 Nov 2026) are enforced by the sending platform as global guardrails outside this blueprint, since event-based entry can't also carry Account-level exclusion conditions.
Worth settling before this is built
  • Should an interest charge of any size qualify someone for this nudge, or only above some minimum outstanding balance? A threshold would materially narrow and sharpen the audience versus a blanket trigger on any INTEREST transaction. Until then: No amount filter applied — any settled, system-generated INTEREST transaction qualifies.
Defaults applied
  • Is 10% the right control-group size here too, or should it differ from the pending-request campaign since this audience is likely much larger? Larger audience could support a smaller holdout % while still giving a usable control sample. Until then: Default to the stated 10% preference.
Limitations
  • Transaction Events is marked new in the platform metadata: proposed, not confirmed as built in production. This campaign depends on it, so it cannot be presented as a verified platform capability.
  • EMI Events is marked new in the platform metadata: proposed, not confirmed as built in production. This campaign depends on it, so it cannot be presented as a verified platform capability.
  • Both EMI Events (EMI_STATUS_CHANGED) and Transaction Events are marked 'new-proposed' — not confirmed built in production. This campaign's entry AND goal both depend on them. If either event isn't actually live, this campaign cannot run as designed at all.
  • Entry cannot exclude customers who already have a Pending or Successful OS-to-EMI request, because Transaction-entry conditions can't reach the EMI Request entity. Some customers may receive both this campaign and the pending-request campaign, or get this one after already converting via another channel.

On screenawaiting-confirmation133.0s
You
I want to increase OS-to-EMI conversions. Design a drip campaign for this.
Agent
Target customers who have already opened an Outstanding-to-EMI (OS-to-EMI) conversion request but haven't completed it, and nudge them to finish before the request expires. The goal is a Successful OS-to-EMI status change, proving the behaviour. Because the request auto-expires after 7 days, the whole sequence is sized to fit inside that window, cheapest channel first, reserving WhatsApp for the final recovery attempt.
Approach
  • Enter on EMI_STATUS_CHANGED where EMI Request Source = OS-to-EMI and New Status = Pending — this is a request that exists but hasn't resolved, which is exactly where a message can still change the outcome.
  • Goal on EMI_STATUS_CHANGED where Source = OS-to-EMI and New Status = Successful, so the platform auto-exits anyone who converts, at any step.
  • Four sends max (the cap), spaced 48h apart (the minimum), finishing by day 6 — inside the 7-day expiry window from P-003, so no message is wasted on an already-expired request.
  • Cheapest-first channel order (EMAIL, SMS, SMS, WHATSAPP), holding WhatsApp back as the higher-cost, higher-visibility last attempt.
  • 10% control group held out per stated preference, so any later read of this campaign has a comparison group rather than relying on raw completion counts.
Considered and not used
  • Entering earlier, at the moment a customer becomes eligible for OS-to-EMI (before any request exists) — No event in this vocabulary scopes reliably to 'eligible for OS-to-EMI specifically' — Outcome Issuance has no entity filter and an unverified status list. Using it risks mixing in unrelated offers. Raised below as a strategic ambiguity instead of guessed at.
  • Branching the journey on Failed vs Expired vs Cancelled to send different recovery copy — The only condition primitive reads a previous send's delivery outcome, not EMI status. Can't be built; flagged as an operational limitation rather than faked with a workaround.
  • A full A/B experiment on messaging variants — Risk appetite is conservative and prefers fewer, better-targeted messages. With message cap 4 and no performance history, splitting further would thin out each arm without a stated hypothesis to test. A plain holdout is enough for now.
  • Using WhatsApp as the first-touch channel for visibility — Conflicts with the stated preference to lead with the lower-cost channel (P-010); EMAIL first, WhatsApp reserved for recovery.
Assumptions
  • EMI Request 'New Status = Pending' represents a conversion that was started but not finalized by the customer, which is the friction point this campaign targets.
  • Quiet hours, DNC and NPA exclusion are enforced by the platform independently of this blueprint's conditions.
  • Customers already in a Failed/Expired/Cancelled state before entry are not re-entered, since entry explicitly requires New Status = Pending.
Worth settling before this is built
  • Should this campaign also reach customers who are eligible for an OS-to-EMI conversion but have never started a request (true top-of-funnel), or stay focused on customers who already have a Pending request open? Changes the audience size and the entire message strategy — top-of-funnel needs awareness/benefit messaging, not a completion nudge. The platform cannot currently scope 'eligible but not started' reliably to OS-to-EMI specifically, so the two designs aren't just a copy change. Until then: Proceed with Pending-request entry only, as designed.
Defaults applied
  • Is EMAIL → SMS → SMS → WHATSAPP the right channel order, or would you prefer WhatsApp introduced earlier for visibility despite the higher cost? Affects cost and perceived urgency pacing across the 4 allowed messages. Until then: Default to cheapest-first with WhatsApp reserved for the final recovery message, per P-010.
Limitations
  • EMI Events is marked new in the platform metadata: proposed, not confirmed as built in production. This campaign depends on it, so it cannot be presented as a verified platform capability.
  • Confirm it's acceptable that the journey cannot detect or react differently to a Failed/Expired/Cancelled status mid-sequence — it can only rely on the 7-day timeout and the automatic goal-exit on Success. If distinguishing 'failed' from 'still pending' mid-journey is important (e.g. to stop messaging someone whose request already failed), that needs a platform capability this blueprint doesn't have today.

goal : {"eventCategory": "EMI Events", "eventType": "EMI_STATUS_CHANGED", "conditions": [{"attribute": "Source", "operator": "Equals", "value": "OS-to-EMI"}, {"attribute": "New Status", "operator": "Equals", "value": "Successful"}]}

How the prompt is put together

The system prompt is the same on every turn. The working brief is not: it is rebuilt each turn from what the conversation has established, so most of its blocks are silent at any one moment. That is usually what explains a turn.

SectionWhat it is responsible for
Role and boundaryThe agent does the business reasoning; application code builds the graph and owns every id.
GROUND RULESNo invented performance numbers, no asserted causes, mock data treated as unverified, hard constraints respected.
HOW TO DESIGN A CAMPAIGNThe method: settle the objective, investigate what could change it, compare candidate architectures, then choose and justify.
QUESTIONS AND OPEN ITEMSHow to ask, what to declare about each question, and what may not be assumed away.
Response contractThe exact JSON shape for ask, request_evidence and propose, including the fields the application later verifies.

How to add a run

Runs are recorded by the drivers, then this page is rebuilt from the records. Nothing is written by hand.

# 1. record a run (writes eval/runs/<label>-<timestamp>/turns/*.json)
node --experimental-strip-types --import ./agent-proto/register.mjs \
     eval/showOne.ts <label>

# 2. optional: describe what changed, so it appears in the change log below
#    eval/runs/<run>/meta.json
#    { "label": "schema", "change": "Mechanism fields enforced", "turns": ["...", "..."] }

# 3. rebuild this page
node --experimental-strip-types --import ./agent-proto/register.mjs \
     docs/buildRunLog.ts
