DimensionBasis gained 'user-belief' (a conjecture about causation, distinct from 'user' which is a fact the business owns); a belief keeps its status but the record permanently appends that it is untested; briefForPrompt computes a DECIDE BEFORE YOU PROPOSE block naming the beliefs by name with two permitted exits; the orchestrator refuses a proposal that builds on a belief while recording no hypothesis anywhere. Scenario A: four of five dimensions classified, two correctly as user-belief, the 25,000 hunch kept as the user's and NOT built, Transaction Amount refused by name. Still proposed on turn 2 (chose the test exit).
dorm2 archived2026-10-14 22:02Adds the broad-cause rule: a stated cause is the user's belief, not a finding, and may be closed exactly two ways — ask which explanation it is, or test them against each other. Accepting it as given is forbidden. Same dormant-card scenario replayed: turn 2 now returns phase=discovery with two targeted follow-ups and two dimensions left open, turn 3 proposes with all five resolved. First run in which a follow-up discovery round actually happened.
dorm archived2026-10-14 21:56Same code as opt2. Contrasting objective (dormant-card reactivation) to check the approach adapts rather than replaying an OS-to-EMI template. Dimensions and option verdicts were genuinely different. GAP FOUND: no follow-up discovery round — it accepted 'they've just forgotten' as a settled cause and built one uniform track, neither asking which kind of forgetting nor testing it.
opt2 archived2026-10-14 21:49Strategic-options step added: the journey step was a flat menu of things to 'consider', so nothing required a verdict and an option never thought about looked identical to one weighed and dismissed. Now names seven options (segmentation, experimentation, branching, fallback, adaptive sequencing, cost/fatigue, measurement), each answerable used / not-applicable / cannot-evaluate, plus a required materially-different alternative. Also fixes the inverted experiment argument (no history is a reason TO test) and adds the converse of the anti-complexity rule (platform capability decides what gets BUILT, never what gets CONSIDERED). OS-to-EMI: experimentation moved from rejected to used.
aud4 archived2026-10-14 21:17Unchanged from aud2/aud3. Dedicated live verification of audience targeting, no code changes beforehand. PASS on all five acceptance criteria: entry uses Statement Due Date and Status only, no Transaction Amount anywhere, the 25,000 threshold stays an attributed user hunch, and the capability gap sits in Limitations with its effect on audience composition.
aud3 archived2026-10-14 21:12Unchanged from aud2. Turn 1 readable with 3 questions; turn 2 failed with a transport error ('fetch failed') at 10.6s. Inconclusive, not a targeting failure.
aud2 archived2026-10-14 21:05No-proxy rule added at the mapping stage (an attribute measuring a different thing at a different grain is not the one they asked for). Turn 1 hit the intermittent empty-response defect, so the run gave no verdict. A knock-on: with no question recorded, turn 2's reply was not counted as an answer and the gate refused.
aud archived2026-10-14 21:00Audience-intent rule added (state intended vs representable audience and the cost of the difference) plus rejected-semantics rule. REGRESSION: readable output, but it closed the targeting gap instead of disclosing it — blueprint entered on Transaction Amount > 25000 and the summary called it an 'outstanding transaction above 25,000'. Failed acceptance criterion 4.
biz archived2026-10-14 20:20Business-dimension-centric discovery: a dimension is defined as a business or customer factor, platform limits may never close one, and the business strategy precedes platform mapping.
live2 archived2026-10-14 19:48Opening and retrieval fix: the first turn must ask for success criteria, briefForPrompt returns the dimension record, and contextChecked is recorded.
final archived2026-10-14 19:29Repeat-tool reliability fix: one all-repeat round no longer withdraws tool use; withdrawal became the bounded fallback at two consecutive repeat rounds. First readable run after five consecutive failures.
att3 archived2026-10-14 19:17Unchanged. Attempt 3 of 3. att2 and att3 showed the terminal round emitting thinking only, with 14 and 25 thinking tokens against a 16,000 cap, which ruled out budget exhaustion.
att2 archived2026-10-14 19:15Unchanged. Attempt 2 of 3.
att1 archived2026-10-14 19:13Unchanged. Controlled reliability diagnostic, attempt 1 of 3. Failed differently: the stream timed out at 180s rather than returning empty.
verify archived2026-10-14 19:03Unchanged from live1. Second verification attempt; failed identically.
live1 archived2026-10-14 18:49Success criteria and measurement added to the strategy, plus the success-settled gate condition. Prompt grew from 10,471 to 11,658 characters.
df2 archived2026-10-14 17:04Discovery gate (C2) + discovery-first prompt (C1) + dimension record. First run under enforcement; the agent still proposed on turn 1 and the gate refused it.
df archived2026-10-14 16:44Pre-gate baseline: discovery-first not yet enforced. The agent proposed a full strategy on turn 1.
osdiag archived2026-10-14 15:48Pre-gate baseline. Re-run with per-round event capture added to the harness only; the application was untouched.

What this page does not tell you

The application can check that a campaign is internally consistent, that two alternatives genuinely differ, and that a claim matches what was built. It cannot judge whether a strategy is a good idea. That still needs a person to read one.
